account-pool-balanced.description: Keep coding across multiple accounts when one reaches its limit. Route Claude Code and Codex threads with quota-aware balancing, primary and reserve accounts, per-account caps, and session affinity. Connect Kimi, Z.AI, OpenCode Go, Cursor, and experimental Devin Local CLI; compatible external clients can use the proxy too. Bring your own provider accounts, subscriptions or API keys. Requires VesnALIA 0.43.1+ and Node/npm; disable VesnALIA's bundled Account Pooler because both register the same routes and command.

acp-profile-icons.description: Recognize eight ACP providers by their brand marks in model pickers and provider controls. Amp and Devin use contrasting theme-colored tiles; other marks follow the theme foreground, with a distinct gray tile for ACP Codex. Requires separately configured ACP providers and VesnALIA 0.44 or newer.

action-topbar.description: Keep open VesnALIA panel tabs within reach above every thread. Search tabs and Actions from one launcher, reorder tabs, close them in place, and drag Actions into panes. Requires VesnALIA 0.40+.

advisor.description: Adds a persistent second-model reviewer to VesnALIA coding threads, with tracked findings and fail-closed review status.

agent-board.description: Follow live VesnALIA agent activity, freshness, completion outcomes and monitoring health. Filter and group visible work by project, repository, provider or status. Optional Ollama Fleet and Redteam add worker visibility. Requires VesnALIA 0.40+; VesnALIA 0.46.0 recommended.

agent-calendar.description: See what your agents worked on and when, as a calendar of work blocks or a weekly time sheet. Each thread gets a block for the time its agent turns ran, colored by project, in a day, 3-day, or week view. Switch to Projects to merge a project's parallel threads into one entry, or open the time sheet to copy hours per thread and day as CSV. Agents can answer "what did my agents work on last week?" with the VesnALIA agent-calendar command and its bundled skill. Turn history stays in a local database on the VesnALIA server and uses no external service.

agent-checklists.description: Keeps a persisted set of agent-owned steps attached to each VesnALIA thread and continues incomplete work automatically.

agent-graph.description: Shows your VesnALIA agents as a live node graph of threads, turns, tool calls, subagents and workflow agents, color-coded by type or status, so you can see what every agent is doing at a glance.

agent-icons.description: Give each VesnALIA agent provider its own icon and colour: built-in glyphs or your own SVG sets, synced across devices.

agent-lanes.description: See which agents are working, waiting for you, or failing across a live timeline. Follow hand-offs between threads, inspect any turn, and approve or reject requests on the block. Open Team lanes beside a thread or run alia lanes now for a text summary. Uses VesnALIA's local thread history, with no external account or API key.

agent-plugins.description: Installs plugins that follow the Agent Plugins spec in VesnALIA, making their skills and approved MCP tools available to Codex and other VesnALIA providers; it is not a Claude marketplace integration.

agent-proxy.description: Runs CLIProxyAPI as a persistent macOS or Linux service, with OAuth account management, provider routing, usage stats, and one-step wiring for Claude Code and Codex.

agent-reload.description: Restart a thread's agent so it picks up MCP servers and config added after the thread started, without losing the conversation. Click the reload button in the thread header, and the agent answers your next message from a fresh session. Agents and scripts can do the same with VesnALIA agent-reload, including an agent reloading itself. Works with Claude Code, Pi, and ACP agents; Codex is not supported.

agent-retry.description: Retry a failed turn instead of accepting it as the end of the work. It retries any failure a provider reports, including one with no error classification at all — a gateway error, a process that died mid-stream, a request refused at the door — which VesnALIA's own retry declines. The wait grows with each attempt, up to 50 by default, and can be scoped by project, provider, thread, or the half of the failure space where the provider never took the request. Every decision is recorded with the rule behind it, and `alia agent-retry log`, `explain` and `simulate` show a retry before or after it happens. Disable VesnALIA's bundled Provider Retry plugin: both queue retries for the same failed turn.

agent-roles.description: Create reusable specialist profiles and start focused agent work. Optional Role Picker and Visual Workflows integrations. Agent work uses your configured provider account and quota.

agent-tools.description: Show which MCP servers and skills each VesnALIA machine actually has, then bring them to one catalogue and one canon. A matrix marks present, missing, and drifted configs; new servers wait for adopt, keep-local, or hide. Sync adds what is missing and never deletes on its own. The Skills tab treats ~/.agents/skills as a git canon, with fan-out into CLI homes and a version archive. Writes back up each config first; loopback paths and local secrets stay on that machine. Optional MetaMCP listing needs that gateway's API key.

agent-traces.description: See where your agents' time goes, from every thread down to each command, tool call, and subagent of a turn. A turn opens as a timeline that splits the agent's time into waiting on you, tools, subagents, thinking, writing, and model time, and it grows live while the agent works. Select a call to see its exit code, output, and arguments, or jump to the reply that followed it in the chat. A Traces page in the sidebar compares your recent threads by active time, calls, and errors, and two turns can be compared phase by phase. Turns export as OpenTelemetry or an HTML snapshot, and the VesnALIA agent-traces command gives agents the same answers. Traces come from the thread history on your VesnALIA server; an OpenTelemetry collector is optional.

agent-tv.description: See what every running agent is doing, and which one needs you, from a live wall at the foot of the sidebar. Each tile shows the tool call in flight, the files touched in the last minute, a 60-second activity trace, and how much of its context window the thread has used. Threads blocked on a question or an approval are marked and sorted to the top. Pop the wall out as a monitor you can drag anywhere in VesnALIA. The VesnALIA agent-tv status command gives terminals and agents the same feed, and nothing leaves your VesnALIA server.

agentic-mermaid.description: Draws Mermaid diagrams in chat with outlined boxes, routed edges, and your theme's colors. Renders 15 diagram types, including gantt, pie, mindmap, timeline, and architecture, through the agentic-mermaid library. Git graphs and types it can't draw keep VesnALIA's own renderer. Diagrams recolor when you switch between light and dark mode. Relies on VesnALIA internals, so a VesnALIA update can return diagrams to the stock renderer until the plugin catches up.

aif-chat.description: Keep research, plans, checks and commits within reach in every VesnALIA thread. A persistent panel tracks tasks, gate results and versions, while buttons launch the next step or a command suggested by your agent. Use the bundled five-step workflow without AI Factory; full AI Factory/AIFHub workflows require separate project installation. Requires VesnALIA 0.48+; the interface is Russian, Windows is verified, and actions use your configured agent's quota or billing.

airbender.description: Keep your project's issues beside the agent doing the work. Track beads or GitHub issues, review plans and results, and start work in branches or worktrees. Run an epic's ready issues in sequence with Autopilot while keeping control of reviews and commits. Requires VesnALIA 0.44+; setup installs bend from GitHub Releases on Linux/macOS amd64 or arm64 using curl and SHA-256 tools, with Go 1.24+ needed for source builds on other platforms.

alium.description: Click anything in VesnALIA without the mouse: press f, type the letter label, and VesnALIA clicks it. Labels cover sidebar threads, pickers, composer controls and hover-only message actions, and most stay one or two letters long. j and k scroll the chat, gg and G jump to its ends, and i puts the cursor back in the composer. Change hint letters, colors and fonts in settings or by asking an agent; changes apply live.

android-emulator.description: Watch and drive an Android emulator, a virtual phone, beside your thread, on the same device your agent controls. The panel streams the live screen with touch, scroll, keyboard and system buttons, and pastes Unicode text into the focused field. Agents list, start and stop AVDs and press keys through VesnALIA android-emulator commands. Needs a Windows or Linux VesnALIA host with the Android SDK and an existing AVD; the plugin installs nothing.

animation.description: Play technical diagrams as a sequence of beats, then export a looping HTML page. Open a .scene.json file to get a stage and a timeline: drag a step boundary to retime it, or click a part to quote its state into chat. Agents write the same JSON with ordinary file edits. GIF and MP4 export are not included; HTML is the shareable output. Requires VesnALIA 0.43 or later.

antigravity.description: Runs VesnALIA threads on Google Antigravity through the agy CLI and ACP adapter, with Gemini 3.x models and native reasoning effort.

antigravity-cli.description: Code with your Antigravity account inside VesnALIA. Choose CLI-discovered models, switch between Plan and Build, and review tool requests in your thread. Requires a separately installed Antigravity CLI and an eligible account; service quota or charges apply. Tested locally on Windows.

antigravity-usage.description: See separate Antigravity weekly quota windows for Gemini and Claude/GPT models in VesnALIA. Reports each model family's quota and reset time from your local Antigravity login. Requires an existing Antigravity ACP provider and a local Antigravity account.

app-preview.description: Detects the app in a thread worktree, starts the detected recipe in a VesnALIA terminal, and can open it in the in-app browser. Ports can share a listener over VesnALIA Connect or send SIGTERM/SIGKILL.

arc-switcher.description: Cycles through your seven most recently opened VesnALIA chats with an Arc-style Command-D switcher.

archive-section.description: Move every thread you archive into an Archived sidebar section, and back to its old section when you unarchive it. The move happens right after the archive, from the sidebar, the CLI, or an agent, and children archived with a parent move too. Threads archived before install, or while the plugin was off, are swept in when it loads. Pick the section by name in settings; emoji and case are ignored, and the section is created if it does not exist.

archived-toggle.description: Show or hide archived threads in the sidebar with one click. An archive button in the sidebar footer adds archived threads to VesnALIA's thread list, and a second click removes them. It flips the same active/archived setting as Organize in the list, so the choice stays after a reload. Requires VesnALIA's built-in Thread list plugin to stay enabled.

artifacts.description: Open your published Claude Code artifacts and Codex Sites from VesnALIA, without going back to the Claude app or ChatGPT. Both lists show as one grid of preview cards, newest first, with a filter; a click opens the item in VesnALIA's browser. An agent can also show an artifact or site in chat as the same card. Reads the Claude Code login from the macOS keychain and the Codex login from ~/.codex/auth.json, and sends them only to api.anthropic.com and chatgpt.com.

asana.description: Work your Asana tickets inside VesnALIA: read them, start an agent thread from one, and hand it back when it's done. Your My Tasks list sits in the sidebar and beside every thread, in your own sections, with overdue and time-against-estimate badges. Opening a task shows its description, images, comments, subtasks, and editable fields, and a thread started from it begins with the ticket's details. Hand back posts your comment and reassigns the task to whoever filed it in one step, and agents need your approval before they write anything to Asana. Needs an Asana account and a personal access token.

asciimoji.description: Give every thread a familiar text face that stays with the conversation. Choose from five generated face families, 12 presets, or custom text through a focused four-tab picker, with thread, project, and global default precedence. Add sidebar faces with adjustable width, theme colors, and expression or marker activity styles plus a live appearance preview; saved choices sync between connected windows. Includes shell controls and needs no external service or account.

attention-sidebar.description: Puts every thread that is waiting on you, from all projects, at the top of the VesnALIA sidebar. Questions and approvals, errors, and finished-but-unread threads share one block, each marked ?, ! or ✓. Running threads get their own block below it, and everything else sits in collapsible project folders with project avatars instead of provider icons. Block titles and labels are in Russian; the plugin is frontend-only and needs no external service.

audio-preview.description: Plays .m4a and other audio files in VesnALIA's file panel, including audio/mp4 that the built-in preview refuses.

auggie.description: Registers Augment Code's Auggie CLI as the acp-auggie provider in VesnALIA.

aura.description: Make your VesnALIA workspace your own with personal wallpapers, animated GIFs, and pixel textures. Save six backgrounds and switch in one click. Choose half or full wallpaper, keep the top bar clean or let the wallpaper continue behind it, and show an optional GitHub activity overview below the New thread composer. Images stay on your VesnALIA server; the activity overview uses the server's GitHub CLI login.

aura-motion.description: Play your own video, GIF or photo behind every VesnALIA conversation, with your messages on frosted glass so they stay readable. MP4 and WebM loops up to 24 MB play at up to 4K, and GIFs up to 8 MB play at their own frame timing. Choose Solid, Glass or Sheer for the message column: dark glass dims bright frames, phones get frosted cards so text stays readable, and Reduce Transparency turns it solid. Add an optional moving pixel-dither effect with seven patterns or five photo motions, and save six backgrounds to switch with one click. Images and videos stay on your VesnALIA server; the optional GitHub activity overview needs the GitHub CLI signed in on that server. A fork of Aura by Mateo Cerquetella; install it instead of Aura, not beside it.

auto-answer.description: Answers an agent's question with one click per question instead of two. A countdown starts the moment you pick an option, then presses the widget's own Next or Submit answer button. It appears under the option you picked and leads with a Stop button, and space or Escape stops it as well. Picking again, another option or the same one, restarts it from the full delay of 4 seconds, adjustable from 1 to 120. It never picks an option and never types free text, and it stands down by itself whenever pressing the button would be wrong, such as nothing selected or the free-text box open.

auto-compact.description: Compacts thread context automatically once usage reaches a configurable percentage, with a manual Compact button in every thread header.

auto-hide-panel.description: Give the thread its full width back when you close the last tab in the right panel. The panel hides itself as soon as its last file or other content tab closes. Info and Diff do not count, and Info you open yourself stays open. Loading the plugin or switching threads never hides the panel.

auto-pin.description: Keeps every thread you start pinned to the top of the sidebar, so a thread stays in reach until you unpin it yourself. Pins each visible top-level thread as it is created, and leaves child threads, hidden threads, and anything already pinned untouched. Unpinning still works the way it always did, so pin state stays yours to edit from the sidebar. Runs on thread creation with nothing to configure, no commands to learn, and no network access.

auto-router.description: Choose a coding model for each task and see where your tokens go. Route work to Codex or Claude Code, delegate helper tasks, and compare recorded usage with cost estimates. Experimental support targets macOS with VesnALIA 0.46.

automation-groups.description: Organize scheduled work into folders and control groups together. Inspect run history, errors and agent transcripts. Requires the bundled Automations plugin; agent runs use provider quota.

automation-palette.description: Run any VesnALIA automation from the quick palette, without opening the Automations page. Each row names the automation and its project, so typing either name finds it, and selecting it starts the run as its schedule would. Every project's automations are listed in every window, and a paused automation keeps its row. Requires VesnALIA 0.42 or later and the VesnALIA CLI on the machine running the VesnALIA server.

autoresearch.description: Orchestrates autoresearch loops: parallel agent workers try code changes, and only the ones your benchmark proves better are kept. The plugin, not the agents, runs every measurement and decides each verdict from paired runs and confidence intervals, with guardrails on secondary metrics. A Live tab shows workers, candidates and each measurement's confidence band as they move, and any study can be replayed. Harvest turns the wins into draft PRs, each with its contribution measured by reverting it. Requires git 2.38 or newer; benchmarks run your repository's own commands, and the GitHub CLI is needed only to publish PRs.

autoresearch-self-loop.description: Let an agent iterate on one measured metric in your Git checkout, and keep a log of every attempt. Each kept run becomes a commit with its result in the message, and a keep is refused when the benchmark or checks failed. A discarded, crashed, or checks-failed run reverts the agent's changes, including new untracked files that Git does not ignore. Needs Git, a committer identity, a clean working tree when a session starts, and a benchmark that prints METRIC name=value lines.

autorouter.description: Routes new VesnALIA threads using task difficulty, live provider quota, benchmark capability, and a configurable cost preference. Each submission first runs a short hidden classification turn on one of your installed providers, which may not be the one the thread ends up on.

aws-activate-usage.description: Keep your AWS promotional-credit runway visible while agents work. View remaining balance, amount used, expiration dates, and current-month allocations in VesnALIA, with cached results when credentials expire. Reconnect an AWS SSO session from the same panel. Requires AWS CLI v2, a configured AWS profile, Billing permissions, and an AWS account with promotional credits.

ayu.description: Adds the three ayu themes (Light, Dark and Mirage) and a settings panel that switches between them and copies any colour from the palette.

backlog.description: Read and edit the Backlog.md files of your VesnALIA projects: a live Kanban board for tasks, and tabs for documents and decisions. Add selected text to the chat of the project with its file path. Needs VesnALIA 0.43 or later with Plugin SDK 0.5.9 or a later 0.5 version, and a Backlog.md folder on an enrolled host. No Backlog CLI or account is needed. Light theme only; tested on macOS.

ballast.description: Know which thread is eating your RAM before the machine starts paging. Reads vm_stat page classes rather than the free percentage macOS reports, which counts inactive pages as free and stays reassuring while the box holds gigabytes of swap — pressure is graded on headroom, paging rate, compression and the kernel's own verdict, and the banner names the signal that decided. Consumers roll up by process tree and by VesnALIA thread, matched through worktree paths, so a 2.4GB row names a thread you can steer instead of six identical node processes. A guard can throttle VesnALIA concurrency, ask the hungriest threads to release memory, stop orphaned processes, or hand the problem to an agent — every one of those is off until you turn it on. Nothing is stopped unless nothing can still be waiting on it, and the apply step takes only ids the plan minted, re-checked against the live process table. macOS and Linux, no account or external service.

bang-shell.description: Run a shell command from a thread's composer and hand the agent the command and its output in one message. Use it when the agent's sandbox or permission mode blocks a command that needs your secrets or access: the agent proposes it, you run it, and the agent only sees the output. Send with Mod+Alt+Enter or Send menu → Run in terminal; the command runs once in the thread's own environment, on whichever machine the session uses, local or remote. You can also highlight a command in an agent's answer and pick Run in terminal next to Add to chat. The message waits in the queue while the command runs, then reaches the agent as a sh block and an output block, so its next answer starts from the real result. Commands that outlast the wait (30 seconds by default) keep running in the thread's Terminal panel, and pagers are off so git log and git diff print in full. Messages from agents, other plugins and VesnALIA thread tell never run a command; commands run with your account's full rights, outside the agent's permission mode. Requires VesnALIA 0.49+.

battery.description: See your laptop's charge in VesnALIA's sidebar without switching to the menu bar. A battery icon and percentage sit at the right end of the sidebar footer, filled red at 20% or less, yellow up to 50% and green above. A click opens a popup with each device's state and charge, including the phone or tablet you opened VesnALIA on when its browser reports a battery. `alia battery status` prints the same reading for terminals and agents. Reads the charge of the machine running the VesnALIA server, which must be a Mac; no account or external service.

beacon.description: See CPU, memory, disk, and processes on the VesnALIA server from the footer. Optional toasts after a minute of high load. Network rates are Linux-only.

beads.description: Track issues and dependencies for long-running agent work with beads, so plans survive context loss. Agents call a beads tool to run bd prime, pick ready work, create tasks under epics, and record status changes in the thread's own checkout. A VesnALIA beads command runs any bd command from your shell. Requires the bd CLI installed separately on the VesnALIA host (brew tap steveyegge/beads && brew install bd).

beautiful-chat.description: Restyles VesnALIA's chat — composer, messages, work rows, loading states — in BeautifulUI's design language, using your active theme's colors.

beside.description: Turns the VesnALIA sidebar into an inbox where threads keep their place and finished work waits on shelves until it has news. Snooze, settle or mute a thread from its row or from VesnALIA's thread menu, and it comes back when it finishes, fails or asks you something. Child threads nest under their parent, and pinned threads drag into your own order. Shelf menus act in bulk with Undo. Optional rules settle threads after you read them, archive long-settled work, or ask a self-hosted decision model whether news needs you. Needs VesnALIA 0.46 or later.

better-latex.description: Renders $...$ and leftover \[...\] / \(...\) math in VesnALIA chat.

boat.description: Run each VesnALIA thread on its own Boat cloud VM that stops when idle and resumes on demand. Start from the stock Ubuntu image or your own saved snapshot, and pick the VM size, Boat environment and org. Requires a Boat account (paid, billed per second) and a VesnALIA hub reachable from the internet.

bookmarks.description: Bookmark any chat message and jump back to it from a Bookmarks tab in the thread's right panel. Clicking a bookmark opens its thread scrolled to the message, however far back it sits. A saved message keeps a filled bookmark button, and a selected passage can be saved as the bookmark's quote. The tab lists bookmarks from every thread, with search and a This thread filter.

bots.description: Adds a Bots panel to the VesnALIA sidebar where you create named bots with their own instructions, provider, model, reasoning level and optional project, then chat with them; each bot's instructions are bound per-thread, so a persona applies only inside that bot's own chats.

bots-sidebar.description: Keep specialist bots, their memory, and their conversations together across projects. Organize chats in activity-aware trees, complete finished work, and move a thread between bots from its header. Route new project conversations to an owner and coordinate bots with @ mentions or attributed messages. Uses your configured VesnALIA providers with no additional service or account. Project-folder creation requires POSIX paths.

branch-graph.description: See how your repositories, branches, worktrees, and VesnALIA threads connect on one canvas. Search across registered Git projects, inspect selected checkouts, and flag detached or prunable worktrees for review. Optional GitHub PR lookup requires the gh CLI and authentication.

breathe.description: An animated pixel wave that guides your breathing while your agent works.

browser-annotate.description: Give your agent page-specific feedback with a screenshot for every annotated element. Select an element in VesnALIA's desktop Browser, write a comment, and send up to 50 annotations together. Review saved comments in the composer and sent message history. Requires VesnALIA 0.43.4 or newer with the desktop Browser.

browser-copy.description: Copies what you point at in a VesnALIA Browser tab: pick any element and get a structured markdown block — page URL, viewport, CSS selector, ARIA role and name, bounds, link, and text — or a PNG of just that element, or a screenshot of the visible tab. One icon button in the thread header opens the three modes, and the picker outlines each target with a hover highlight and label as you move. Redaction is a heuristic on form fields — a password input, or a name, id or autocomplete matching password, credential, secret, token, api-key or auth — so it covers more than passwords but nothing outside an input, and images are not redacted.

browser-gestures.description: Swipe two fingers on the trackpad to go back and forward in the VesnALIA browser. A dark arrow slides in from the edge as you swipe, and the page changes when you lift your fingers; pull back to cancel. Vertical scrolling and horizontal scrollers that can still move keep working as before. Requires the VesnALIA desktop app and a trackpad.

browser-session-import.description: Signs every ordinary VesnALIA Browser tab into one imported cookie session. Import once from a local Chrome, Firefox, or other browser profile, or from a JSON cookie export, and the shared session carries those logins to existing and new tabs. Re-import any time to replace the session, and remove it with one button to clear the Browser. Cookies are read on this machine only; native profiles read on macOS and Linux, while JSON exports work anywhere the VesnALIA desktop runs.

browser-tools.description: Test websites from your agent and inspect what actually happened in the browser. Navigate, click and type using page snapshots, then review screenshots and browser errors. Requires VesnALIA 0.43 or later with a connected desktop browser and an agent provider; normal provider and website-account costs apply. Tested on macOS; other host operating systems remain unverified.

browserbase.description: Browserbase gives VesnALIA a real browser to use the web like a human. Navigate interactive websites, perform complex actions using natural language, and extract data from pages. Each VesnALIA thread gets its own cloud browser session. Requires a Browserbase account and API key; usage counts toward your Browserbase plan.

btrfs-cow.description: Start a thread with your installed dependencies, build caches, and uncommitted changes already in place. Each thread gets an independent checkout that shares disk blocks until files change, using Btrfs snapshots or reflink copies. Select Btrfs Cow in the environment picker; the plugin checks filesystem support on the chosen machine. Requires Linux, Git, GNU cp with reflink support, and a compatible filesystem such as Btrfs or XFS; snapshot mode also needs the btrfs command.

bureaucat.description: Bring assigned and project tasks into your VesnALIA workflow. Sort and filter complete task lists, inspect details, update supported task fields, and prepare agent drafts. Requires an authenticated Bureaucat CLI and configured service URL; complete scans are limited to 5,000 tasks.

burn.description: See what every agent thread costs in dollars while it runs, per prompt and across all your threads. A chip beside the context circle shows the thread's total and what the last prompt added; click it for where the money went, a chart of every model call and the total with child threads. The Burn tab in the side panel lists the cost of each prompt, and a Burn page in VesnALIA's navigation charts spend across threads by day, project, model and harness. Budgets notify you at 80% and 100% of a thread's budget, and stop a run only if you turn that on. Works with pi, OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code and any harness that reports usage to VesnALIA; where a harness records no cost, Burn estimates it from list prices and marks it with ~.

cache-watch.description: See how much prompt caching each turn reuses and what its tokens would cost at Standard API rates. Expand the Cache panel for per-request reads and writes, first-request cache use, and estimated time left. Open the Cache marker under an assistant reply for saved turn details, or Session statistics for totals and turn history. Optional time-limited keepalive sends ordinary paid turns through your configured provider; cache hits and savings are not guaranteed. Requires VesnALIA 0.48+ and Plugin SDK 0.6.104+; Claude Code Telemetry support requires that separate provider plugin.

callstack.description: Agents publish call-stack flow diagrams — types moving through calls, with conditions, loops, and before/after change markers — into a live thread panel with tree, diagram, and swimlane views, drift tracking against the workspace, inline code snippets, and diffs.

calm.description: A little world while your agent works. Sixteen pixel-art scenes bring sheep, sailboats, a rooftop cat, and forty-eight little misadventures to VesnALIA. An amber light means it needs you. A rain cloud marks an error. Requires VesnALIA 0.45 or later, with no external service or account.

canvas.description: Gives every thread a shared tldraw canvas that agents draw diagrams on, animate as a step-by-step walkthrough, and read back — including the shapes you add yourself.

captains-deck.description: Puts a first mate's whole crew on one board, so you only touch the calls that need you. Five columns track what is charted, what is underway, the decisions waiting on you, merges, and landings. Answer a call in place: pick an option, add a note, and the answer reaches the first mate's thread. Cards carry live thread state (working, queued, needs input, failed), the worker bot, and the pull request link. The first mate charts and moves work with the `alia deck` command; no external service or account is needed.

career-hub.description: Keep every application and its tailored CV in one place. Build a complete career profile from multiple CVs and reusable interview stories. Tailor concise CVs with a reference document's section order, then save versions and download PDFs. The optional embedded assistant uses your configured VesnALIA provider and its normal quota or charges.

cascade.description: Shows active VesnALIA threads in a tiled layout with horizontal columns and vertical groups.

catchup.description: Shows a short recap above the composer, so you can pick up a thread without rereading it. Close it with × once you have read it; it stays closed on every device until a newer recap replaces it. Recaps follow the language of your latest messages, or one language you set. Other layouts add a compact banner, an expanded banner and a larger card. Each recap is a normal request to the provider you choose and never enters the thread's context.

change-gate.description: Approve production changes from a card that says what changes, where and how to undo it. Agents ask before a migration, a deploy or deleting shared data, and you answer with one click. An approval covers one request, and a decline tells the agent not to look for another route. Every decision stays in a journal page and in VesnALIA change-gate log. Agents are instructed to ask; the gate does not block other tools.

chat-dock.description: Write your next message beside the diff, file or tab you are reading: the composer moves into the right panel while it is open. Your draft and the cards above the box (running commands, child threads, questions) move with it and go back under the timeline when you close the panel. Dock it as a strip under whichever tab is open, or as a Chat tab of its own that splits and drags like any other. Split chat panes keep a composer each, and on a phone it docks at the bottom of the panel drawer. It moves VesnALIA's own page elements, which are not a documented interface, so a VesnALIA update may need a plugin update. Requires VesnALIA 0.48 or later.

chat-find.description: Press Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on Mac) in any VesnALIA chat to find words in the conversation, with every match highlighted where it appears. Enter and Shift+Enter step through matches, and the chat scrolls each one clear of the composer, including matches inside bold text, links, and syntax-highlighted code. The count updates while an agent is still replying, without losing your place. Escape closes the bar and puts the cursor back where it was. It searches the messages the chat has loaded, leaves Ctrl+F to the embedded browser and terminals when they have focus, and needs no account or external service.

chat-search.description: Find any word in the chat you are reading and see every occurrence highlighted in the messages themselves. A Find in chat tab in the thread panel lists each hit with context, and Enter steps through them while the current one glows brighter. Hits cover the whole thread, including messages scrolled far out of view, and highlights follow new messages as they stream in. Match case, regular expressions, a Mod+Shift+F shortcut, and a VesnALIA chat-search command for agents are included. Runs locally with no external service.

chat-sidebar.description: See which threads need you at a glance in a messenger-style sidebar with live status, folders, and project colours. Sub-agents and forks fold into their parent, so each task is one row. Attention, project, and section folders sit as tabs or a Telegram-style rail, each with unread badges, and you can add your own folders that pick chats by status, project, agent, or words in the title. Projects get distinct colours you can change, and the + starts a chat in the open project. Search, pinned order, splits, and VesnALIA's thread shortcuts all keep working.

chat-width.description: Give your conversations the room they need. Save separate Reading and Wide widths, or fill the current pane. Messages and the input stay aligned across split views and side panels. Preferences stay in this browser; no account or external service is required.

chatgpt-skin.description: Dress VesnALIA in the ChatGPT desktop app's look, from the canvas and sidebar down to every button state, in light and dark. Both palettes ship, so switching modes changes the light and not the layout. Hover, active, focus-visible, and disabled states are themed across buttons, menu rows, tabs, switches, chips, and icon buttons. Menus, dialogs, popovers, tooltips, and the command palette share one surface ramp, and matching code themes carry the palette into syntax highlighting. No account and no network request: VesnALIA reads the stylesheet straight from the plugin directory.

chief.description: Coordinates project supervisors that delegate work to managed worker and reviewer threads and follow it through completion.

chime.description: Plays configurable notification sounds when VesnALIA turns start, finish, fail, pause for a question, or request approval.

claude-account-switcher.description: Switches one VesnALIA Claude Code thread to the verified Claude subscription login on its machine while preserving thread history.

claude-accounts.description: Switch Claude Code or Codex logins when quota runs out, and start a new VesnALIA thread with a saved account. Check remaining limits before choosing an account, or add one through the provider's browser sign-in. Runs on macOS and Windows, with snapshots stored in Keychain or encrypted with Windows DPAPI; tokens go to Anthropic and OpenAI, while Cursor and other providers show limits only. Requires provider accounts; Codex switching also needs the Codex CLI signed in with ChatGPT, and saving Codex logins on macOS needs Xcode Command Line Tools.

claude-auth.description: Authenticate Claude Code CLI remotely or on mobile via Tailscale, inspect token expiration, and renew sessions.

claude-switcher.description: See every Claude Code account in one usage panel, pick the account before a new thread's first message or from any thread's header, start new projects on the best account, and move a project to a free account when a turn hits a subscription limit. Runs on macOS and Linux, on the machine that holds your Claude Code logins.

claude-theme.description: Give VesnALIA terracotta accents with charcoal dark and off-white light palettes. Select one palette that follows Light, Dark or System, with matching syntax and terminal colours. Adapted from SK's Claude Theme for VS Code, with accents on selected navigation and active tabs. Requires VesnALIA 0.47.1 or later and a compatible Plugin SDK; no account or external service is needed.

claude-usage.description: See how much of your Claude plan is left and where your AI coding spend went, by session, day and model, across every agent CLI you use. Each limit window shows what is left, when it resets and where you will land at your current pace, with a plain verdict on whether there is room for a big task. Sessions carry their titles and projects; open one for its models and its cost by token type, or click a model to filter the whole page. Reads Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and the other CLIs ccusage supports from their local logs, and draws each provider in its own colour. Prices come from LiteLLM's public price list, so a newly released model is priced without a plugin update. Plan limits use the Claude Code sign-in already on your machine and need a Claude subscription.

cli-agents.description: Start each chat with a specialist agent or selected profile instructions. Choose native Claude Code and OpenCode agents, or Codex profile developer instructions (up to 4096 characters; other profile settings are not applied), in new chats and handoffs on local or enrolled remote machines. Requires VesnALIA 0.43.0 or later on macOS or Linux and an installed, authenticated supported CLI; provider subscription limits or API charges apply.

clickable-local-link.description: Opens a local document from a chat link in its Mac app, and a folder link in Finder, with one click. Text and code files keep VesnALIA's preview, and Option-click selects any linked item in Finder. Scripts, apps and unknown file types are only selected, never opened, including when a link hides them behind a symlink. A bundled skill tells agents to write local paths as clickable links. Works in the macOS desktop app on the Mac that runs VesnALIA.

close-tab.description: Keep the preview down to the files you still need, and close each tab like in a browser instead of aiming at a tiny ×. Double-click or middle-click a tab you have read; on a Mac trackpad a three-finger click works too. Control+W and a palette command close the active tab, because ⌘W closes the window. A × at the right of the preview header hides the panel when you are back to the chat.

cloud-sandbox.description: Creates VesnALIA machines on Vercel Sandboxes from reusable templates that bake in tooling and inject agent credentials at creation, so a remote machine is ready to run threads without manual setup.

code-review.description: Lists the GitHub pull requests awaiting your review, runs your own review skills over one in a VesnALIA thread, and turns what it finds into individual review comments you edit and post yourself, each shown beside the code it refers to.

code-review-workspace.description: Understand a pull request or local diff before you approve it, and post a review you edited from an agent's draft to GitHub. An agent splits the change into chapters in reading order, rates each one's risk, and points to the one to three lines most likely to hide a defect. The review agent drafts line comments with a severity, a summary, and a suggested verdict, and you choose what posts to GitHub. All reviews sorts your PRs by whose turn it is, and after new commits Since your review shows only what changed and checks each of your earlier comments. Review a VesnALIA thread's uncommitted work the same way, then send your comments back to the thread that wrote the code. Needs git and a signed-in GitHub CLI (gh) on the VesnALIA server, works with github.com only, and spends your VesnALIA agent provider's usage on guides and reviews.

codex-migrate.description: Keep your existing Codex projects and chats together in VesnALIA. Preview selected folders and follow the import progress for each one. Preserve conversations, available attachments, dates, and archive state with a VesnALIA database backup before changes. Requires VesnALIA 0.44, Git, and a separate Codex CLI installation on the same computer.

codex-realtime.description: Run Voice Mode's voice chats on your ChatGPT subscription instead of a separately billed OpenAI API key. It hands Voice Mode the ChatGPT sign-in that the Codex CLI already keeps on the machine running the VesnALIA server, reads it again for every chat, and never renews or rewrites it. Only the plugins you allow, Voice Mode to begin with, receive the token; the VesnALIA app, the command line and agents in threads never do. This is an undocumented use of the subscription that OpenAI could stop accepting at any time, nobody has checked whether OpenAI's terms allow it, and voice chats count against your ChatGPT plan. Requires VesnALIA 0.46 or later, Voice Mode 0.1.9 or later, and the Codex CLI signed in with Sign in with ChatGPT on a plan that includes Codex.

codex-theme.description: Brings the OpenAI Codex / ChatGPT desktop app's look to VesnALIA: system-font typography at 430 weight, the Codex surface and menu geometry, its send arrow, and a roomier left rail. Pick Catppuccin or VesnALIA's own colors, and turn on optional changes in the plugin settings. Light and dark.

collapsible-navigation.description: Folds the sidebar navigation upward into a compact strip to maximize vertical space for your thread list. Quick actions remain accessible with one click in the collapsed bar, and navigation icons can optionally move into the window top header. Remembers expanded and collapsed state across restarts.

color-swatches.description: Shows a color chip beside CSS values in messages, code, and diffs, so you can recognize colors without copying them into another tool.

command-center.description: Boards every dispatched request and open question as a card, lets you reply or comment on an agent's work straight from the board, and sends macOS notifications when a card's status changes. Includes Chief: one global Chief, a project chief per project, and task architects, for routing dispatched work through an org instead of a flat worker thread. Requires the Tasks plugin — the board offers a one-click install if it isn't already there, but never installs it silently — and, for voice input, microphone access. If you also run the `notify` plugin, expect two macOS banners for overlapping events — this one fires on board-card status, `notify` on thread lifecycle.

command-code.description: Runs VesnALIA threads on any of Command Code's 70 coding models, so a bug has to survive reviewers on Claude, GPT, GLM, Kimi or DeepSeek without leaving VesnALIA. Shell commands, file reads and edits arrive as VesnALIA timeline cards with streamed output and diffs, and reasoning stays separate from the reply. Needs Command Code installed and signed in, plus the adapter this repository ships. Command Code's headless mode cannot prompt per tool call, so writes are one setting rather than a per-call approval.

compact-nav.description: Make more room for threads with compact, borderless sidebar icons. Keep your saved order and hidden destinations, with controls to rearrange or show them. Hover labels and selected states keep navigation recognizable. Requires VesnALIA 0.42+ and Plugin SDK 0.4.53+, with no extra service or account.

compact-panes.description: Fit more threads and pane content on screen with tighter spacing and a composer that stays put. Reduce sidebar, header, tool-card and composer spacing. Choose a preset, custom color, monochrome or saved per-project colors, with controls for sidebar accents. Compact sizing targets desktop widths with a fine pointer; requires VesnALIA 0.42+ and uses internal styling hooks.

compact-rail.description: Make more room on a small desktop screen with compact navigation and narrower window gutters. Use a 40 px navigation rail with full-size icons and frame gutters at 60% of their default size. Resize the thread sidebar while its list fills the available width. Requires VesnALIA 0.46+ and Plugin SDK 0.6.37+; applies to desktop widths with a fine pointer and uses internal layout selectors.

companion-chat.description: Opens a fresh hidden thread beside the current VesnALIA conversation with independent provider and model selection, keeping it out of the sidebar unless the user later makes it visible.

composer-autocollapse.description: Keep the prompt box compact when you click away or leave it idle, with drafts left in place. Set the focus-out delay and idle timeout, while editor, toolbar, model-picker and menu interactions stay open. Idle collapse requires focus inside the box and an empty draft, or a hidden tab when that option is enabled. Requires VesnALIA 0.49.0+.

composer-predictions.description: Suggests the message you're likely to send next as ghost text in the empty composer, one Tab from an editable draft. Nothing is sent for you: Tab only fills an empty message box, and typing, pasting or Escape hides the suggestion until the conversation moves on. Suggestions are saved across restarts and checked against the conversation before they reappear, so an unchanged thread costs no new request. Every reply in a thread you've opened costs one request in a hidden helper thread, which receives up to 48,000 characters of recent messages and tool output.

conductor-theme.description: Applies the Conductor workspace aesthetic across VesnALIA with roasted espresso and native black surfaces, warm brown message cards, bone typography, and emerald accents.

context-handoff.description: Track context usage as a percentage and safely continue long tasks in fresh threads. A meter above the chat input shows how full the context window is: it uses your theme's main color below 20% (light gray in dark mode), then turns yellow at 20%, orange at 30%, red at 40% and dark red at 65%. Each thread has an Auto handoff switch, off until you turn it on. Turn it on below 20% and the thread hands off once it reaches 30%; turn it on at 20% or above and it hands off at the next safe stopping point. The agent saves its plan and progress as notes, and a fresh thread confirms it read them, then continues with the switch on. Turning the switch off cancels a pending handoff.

context-health.description: See what contributes to your thread’s context usage. Search recorded text, inspect observed skill reads and browse available skills. Optional Codex session detail reads logs on the thread host; no separate account or paid service is required.

context-meter.description: Keeps threads in the smart zone, by tracking context against a limit you set rather than the provider's full window.

copilot-aic-usage.description: Track Copilot AI credits in your VesnALIA thread. See this session's usage, today's host total, and monthly premium requests. Install the GitHub Copilot provider from VesnALIA's marketplace and sign in to GitHub Copilot CLI with a Copilot-enabled account.

copilot-session-credits.description: Track reported GitHub Copilot credit usage for each VesnALIA thread. Click the indicator to see the amount, coverage, and capture status or get Pi setup instructions. Copilot CLI works directly with the official registry provider and supported custom variants; Pi requires a separate companion extension and Pi 1.5.0+. Requires authenticated GitHub Copilot access; tested on macOS. Pi coverage is partial, so earlier calls and hidden retries may be missing.

copilot-usage.description: See GitHub Copilot AI-credit or premium-request usage beside your other VesnALIA providers. Reads the quota shown by the authenticated Copilot CLI and reports the billing-cycle reset estimate. Requires GitHub Copilot CLI, a Copilot account, and tmux on the VesnALIA host.

copy-session-id.description: Copy a thread's session ID from its left-sidebar context menu.

cortado.description: Neutral graphite with warm orange and amber, in light and dark. Three palettes: one that follows VesnALIA's light or dark mode, and fixed dark and light versions. Recolors the app, the syntax colors in chat, diffs and file previews, and the terminal.

crew.description: Run a standing team of agents that message each other, hand off work and wait for you only when they need an answer. You describe the team once in a crew.yaml: each member gets a fixed address, its own provider and model, a role and its own worktree, and every member is a thread in the sidebar. Several crews in one project coordinate through their leads, VesnALIA Tasks and the base branch, with a step limit so they cannot loop forever. A project overview shows who works, who waits and every cross-crew message. Merge and rebase need the repository on the machine VesnALIA runs on.

ctrl-enter-send.description: Send messages with the shortcut you choose: Ctrl+Enter, Enter, or Shift+Enter. Use the same choice in new threads, replies, queued messages, and sent-message editors. Hover over the send button to see the active shortcut; Ctrl+Enter mode also accepts Command+Enter on macOS. Requires VesnALIA 0.46+.

cua-driver.description: Gives VesnALIA agents background desktop and Chromium browser control, powered by the open-source Cua Driver from Cua AI, with per-provider routing.

cursor-sidebar.description: See at a glance which agents are working, which need an answer and which are done, with spawned chats nested under their parent. Group chats by project, last update, status or environment, or draw one flat list, and narrow every grouping to one project from the switcher. With the Projects plugin, a worker opens as a tab of its project lead, so the lead's side panel stays in view. After install the sidebar switches to the Cursor navigation layout, and Compact is one setting away. Give each project a glyph in one of ten colours or an uploaded PNG, filter by status, age, environment or pull request, and spot chats on cloud machines by their cloud mark. Needs VesnALIA 0.49 or newer; no account or external service.

dashboard.description: Keep project conversations, live activity and application shortcuts in one workspace. Read and continue chats, search project history and switch conversations with bottom tabs. Track work and requests for attention across projects, open applications alongside your workspace and choose English or Russian. Requires VesnALIA 0.48+ and internet access for first-install dependencies; no separate service, account or API key.

decisions.description: Gets a probability for a typed question, and keeps the TypeSafe API key in one place. A thread or another plugin sends state and questions and gets probabilities back. The Decisions page shows ask counts, callers, cost, and yes/no confidence for 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days. Named asks stay in the plugin database, and the inbox sends the ask marked in use. A TypeSafe API key is required, and the page prices input tokens at $0.042 per million.

deepseek-harness.description: Run DeepSeek Harness (dsh) threads in VesnALIA over ACP, with Standard, Creator, and Minimal modes chosen in the New thread composer, a read-only badge naming the mode a thread booted with, a live roster of the dsh subagents a thread deploys, harness slash commands exposed to the agent, and one-command provisioning of the dsh profiles, run_command plugin, and ACP bridge patch. Requires dsh installed globally and a model credential for its route.

dependabot.description: Reviews GitHub Dependabot alerts grouped by dependency and sends grouped fixes to VesnALIA agents.

design-director.description: Catch a screen that looks generic before you call the work done, and keep every design score on record. A critic scores each screenshot without seeing the code, so the agent that built the screen is not the one grading it. Three tiers run from a single-call spot check after any UI change to a full redesign with seeded directions and critic rounds. Critic runs spend tokens on your own provider account, at a cost that depends on the model you pick, and the screenshot scripts need Chrome or Chromium and Node 18 or newer.

desktop-browser-agent.description: Lets your agents use the apps and browser tabs on your machine in the background, while you keep working. Agents read and operate native apps and Chrome, Edge or Brave windows through Cua Driver from Cua AI, which the settings page installs and checks on each machine. The optional Browser Bridge for VesnALIA extension lets them work in any tab of your signed-in browser, in an Agent tab group you can pause. Tools that run code or force-quit apps start off, and agents can be made to ask before clipboard, screen capture and file actions. Needs Cua Driver (free, MIT). Tested on macOS 14+; Windows 10/11 and Linux with X11 are supported by Cua Driver but not yet tested with this plugin.

devin.description: Run coding tasks with Devin from a VesnALIA thread. Devin appears in the provider picker, and VesnALIA discovers models from the local ACP session while rendering responses, tool calls, and file changes. Install the Devin CLI and authenticate it on each VesnALIA host with `devin auth login`.

diagram-fences.description: Draws PlantUML, Graphviz, D2 and the rest of the Kroki diagram family in chat and in Markdown file previews. Mermaid stays with VesnALIA. PlantUML and D2 install from the plugin's settings screen; Graphviz uses dot when it exists and a bundled WASM renderer otherwise. Diagrams go to kroki.io only when no local engine can draw them, and a self-hosted Kroki URL can replace it. Diagram source is capped at 64 KB and every render is cached.

dictation-shortcuts.description: Dictate into a VesnALIA draft by holding Space, then release to finish. Enter finishes recording without sending, Escape cancels, and Ctrl+Shift+Space toggles recording without holding a key. Microphone tooltips and modifier-held badges show the controls beside VesnALIA’s native buttons. Requires VesnALIA 0.46.1+, microphone permission and an available VesnALIA voice-input service; that service’s existing account requirements and charges still apply, with no additional speech service installed.

diff-explorer.description: Review every changed file in one scroll, and ⌘-click any symbol to read its definition without leaving the diff. Press Ctrl+- to step back, so you can follow a call several levels deep and return to the hunk you were reading. Switch between uncommitted changes and all changes since the base branch. Open it with ⌘⇧D or the button in the thread header. Go to definition needs the language server on your PATH: gopls, rust-analyzer, pyright, clangd, or sourcekit-lsp; TypeScript downloads typescript-language-server through npx on first use.

diff-plus.description: Improves VesnALIA's Diff tab with a folder tree beside the file list: file counts and +/- per folder, sticky folders, Tree or Flat view, compact folders, a view synced with the list, and your recent commits in the scope picker. It works through the tab's own filter, so VesnALIA's search, Viewed marks, split view and Add to chat work as before. Requires VesnALIA 0.48 or later; it finds the Diff tab by its page structure, so a VesnALIA update may need a plugin update.
