diff-review.description: Comment on a thread's changes line by line, then send the comments to its agent, which fixes the code and answers each one. A Review tab beside the thread shows the diff of its uncommitted, staged or unstaged changes, its branch, one commit or a range, and each comment follows its code as the code moves. The same tab reviews a GitHub pull request: answer its threads, mark files viewed in step with GitHub, and submit your comments as one review, posted as the GitHub CLI's signed-in account. An AI review leaves comments of its own, @reviewer answers a question inside a comment thread, and Fix in a new thread hands the comments to another agent; these runs start as threads under the one being reviewed, in the permission mode set in the settings (VesnALIA's Approve for me by default, or Accept edits), and in full permission mode with a provider that lacks that mode, such as opencode. Follows the review loop of the open-source diffity, credited in the plugin's third-party notices. Needs VesnALIA 0.48 or later with VesnALIA's Git plugin on, and the signed-in GitHub CLI (gh) for pull request review only; it is built on experimental VesnALIA plugin APIs that may change between VesnALIA releases.

diff-tree.description: Review Git changes by folder and bring selected code into your VesnALIA chat. Compare branch changes, the working copy, recent commits, or a single commit in unified or split view. Expand unchanged context and add file mentions without sending the draft. Requires VesnALIA 0.46.1+, SDK 0.6.49+, and Git on the workspace host; no external service or account is needed.

diff-viewed.description: See how much of a long diff you've read, with a viewed count beside VesnALIA's own Viewed checkboxes and the same marks on GitHub. The changes panel toolbar counts the files you have checked, such as 3/6 viewed, across every file in the range. On a thread with an open pull request, checking a file in VesnALIA marks it viewed on GitHub, and a file marked viewed on GitHub is checked in VesnALIA. A file with edits you have not pushed shows a Local icon until a push makes its diff match the pull request's. Requires VesnALIA 0.47 or later, and GitHub sync needs the gh CLI signed in.

diffdad.description: See only the pull requests that ask for you by name, and read each one as a narrated review instead of a raw diff. The sidebar page lists your direct review requests with criticality tags, approvals, verdict, and age, sorted the way Diff Dad's own queue is, with a repo filter. An All tab embeds Diff Dad's command center, and a thread panel action opens the thread's own pull request review. Agents get a diffdad_review tool that returns a PR's verdict, TL;DR, and concerns as text. Requires Diff Dad's daemon running locally with its own GitHub token and AI provider, and the GitHub CLI logged in.

discord.description: Run alia agent threads from Discord, answer approvals, and manage your server with permission-gated tools. Start a dedicated conversation with a bot mention and receive final answers in its Discord thread. Choose the project, machine, model, and permission mode in VesnALIA. Requires a Discord bot with Message Content Intent and a configured VesnALIA agent provider.

disk-usage.description: Shows what's taking up disk space on the VesnALIA server host, ncdu-style, with drill-down by directory and a VesnALIA disk-usage CLI.

doc-review.description: Comment on documents, spreadsheets, and web pages beside the chat, then hand every comment to an agent in one message. Select text in Markdown, PDF, Word, or PowerPoint files, box a chart on a page or slide, pick spreadsheet cells, or click any element of an HTML page; a comment on an area reaches the agent with an image of that region. Draw over a prototype or page to cross out a button, frame a block, or point an arrow to where it should move, and the agent gets the page as you saw it with your strokes on top. Each comment shows whether the agent closed it with a note on what changed or answered with a question, and a thread under it carries the conversation for as many rounds as it takes. In the VesnALIA desktop app, a Review button beside the browser's address bar puts the same comments on a live site, where they stay on their pages across reloads and deploys. Download a PDF with your comments as annotations any PDF viewer shows; Doc Review in another VesnALIA imports them, so a colleague can answer and send the file back. Files attached to chat messages open in the same tab, and the tab works in VesnALIA's mobile web app. Needs poppler-utils and LibreOffice on the machine the VesnALIA server runs on; Chrome or Chromium there adds the pictures of drawings on HTML pages.

dockside.description: Organizes VesnALIA threads into compact project-first families with semantic status, inline child agents, persistent drag ordering, and mobile active-thread navigation.

drmanhattan.description: Makes agents in parallel threads take turns on builds and tests, and shows each thread its queued runs. Threads on a machine with drmanhattan, a local job queue, are told to run heavy commands through it, so several agents stop compiling at the same time and slowing each other down. While a thread has runs going, a row above its composer shows each run's slot or place in line against its usual time, with a cancel button and a link to its log; the Info tab lists recent results. A drmanhattan page in VesnALIA's navigation shows the queue on every connected machine, each run linked to the thread that queued it, and archiving a thread stops the dev servers it started. Agents and scripts also get VesnALIA drmanhattan runs, status and cancel. Needs the free, open-source drmanhattan command-line tool on each machine (macOS or Linux); the drmanhattan page installs and starts it with one click, showing the commands first.

droid.description: Registers Factory.ai's Droid CLI as the acp-droid provider in VesnALIA.

dynamic-file-tree.description: Browse the active project beside every VesnALIA thread, with Git status, previews, diff counts, and live agent activity. Navigate files and folders scoped to the current Environment or Worktree. Preview text, Markdown, and image files inside VesnALIA. See reads, writes, added, deleted, and changed files with configurable colors and metadata. Requires VesnALIA 0.48+ and a thread with an available Environment; it uses no external service or account.

e-corp.description: Turns VesnALIA into a cold corporate workstation, lit by one continuous petroleum-blue field that every panel shares. Dark and light are the same room at two exposures, so switching modes changes the light and not the design. Bundled Pierre-compatible code themes carry the palette into code, diffs, the file tree, and the terminal, with separate focus, selection, warning, and destructive colours. IBM Plex Sans and Mono and the texture are embedded in the stylesheet, so the theme makes no network requests.

elephant-goldfish.description: Runs a fresh-context review on every Markdown spec and applies only the changes you explicitly approve. Spec files stay as plain Markdown in your project checkout, listed on a dedicated spec workspace page and in a tab beside each conversation. Seven agent skills cover the workflow from brainstorm and draft through staged reviews, findings and proposals to resolution and drift reports. Reviews run as VesnALIA workers on the provider configured for the reviewed project, or as a tool-less OpenAI-compatible endpoint that needs a base URL, model id and API key.

emoji-react.description: Answer an agent with one click: pick an emoji reaction and it drafts your reply. Select text in a reply to quote it with your reaction from the selection menu, or use the reaction buttons under each message. Turn on smart reactions and the agent adds reactions that fit its question, such as SQLite or Postgres, as buttons in its reply. Smart reactions add a short instruction to each thread.

env-catalog.description: Store API keys, tokens, and secrets in a single encrypted catalog across all VesnALIA sessions and machines. Securely request credentials via masked in-app modals. Agents automatically check available credentials before prompting you, and persist newly provided keys on demand. Values are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM and synchronized via your central VesnALIA server. Includes dedicated agent tools, a full-featured management UI with .env import/export, and terminal CLI commands.

extella.description: Lets agents reuse programs that earlier threads already wrote: search them by meaning, run them on your machine, save new ones. A thread that asks in different words still finds the saved program and runs it without writing code. Programs run on your computer through Extella Desktop and can read local files there; a run takes about 10 seconds. Later threads and other VesnALIA projects that use the same Extella agent see the same library. Needs an Extella account with an API key and agent id, and Extella Desktop on the machine that runs programs.

factory.description: Turn requests into reviewed pull requests: a Lead plans tasks, specialist agents build them, and independent agents review each PR. A Factory page in the left rail shows every agent's live status and a board from Backlog to Done. When a builder finishes, the Lead opens a draft PR; Reviewer 1 and a Security reviewer start within about two minutes, plus Reviewer 2 for large or sensitive diffs, and each posts its verdict on the PR. The PR is marked ready for review only when every reviewer approves, and merging stays with you. Needs a Git project, the agent CLIs you choose per role (Claude Code, Codex or Cursor), and a GitHub remote with the gh CLI for PR review; optional Rafter scans need a Rafter account.

factory-droid.description: Use Factory Droid as a native agent provider in VesnALIA: live model catalog, reasoning controls, and autonomy mapping over ACP.

fast-archive.description: Archive finished conversations from the thread header. Uses VesnALIA’s archive and restore behavior, and avoids duplicate buttons when native archiving is present.

fast-split.description: Open a neighboring New thread pane from the sidebar footer. Keep the current pane visible while starting another conversation. Available in wide layouts, up to VesnALIA’s pane limit.

fat-fingers.description: Makes every icon in VesnALIA 50% larger on your phone, so a thumb has something to see and something to hit. Applies under the same phone test VesnALIA uses for its own touch sizing, so a desktop window with a mouse is left exactly as it was. Scales the icon's layout box rather than painting it larger, so the button around it grows to fit. Leaves diagrams and images inside messages at their normal size. Works in the VesnALIA mobile app and in a phone browser, with nothing to configure and no network access.

feature-flags.description: See and manage LaunchDarkly feature flags from the VesnALIA sidebar: toggle each flag per environment and filter by maintainer, status, type, and tag.

feed.description: See every thread that needs your answer in one list, each with a one-line summary of its latest result. Rows sort into Needs your response, In progress, and Paused, and you reply, pause, archive, or move a thread from its row. A bundled manager skill starts new work in a section the Feed watches and flags child results for you. Summaries use your Codex login (ChatGPT account or OpenAI API key); without it, a row shows the first sentence of the agent's latest message.

file-explorer.description: Keeps a file explorer pinned to any project or thread while you switch between VesnALIA threads. Search by file name or path and jump the tree to matches, including bare file names resolved across configured search roots. Search and replace text inside files under the pinned root with case, whole-word, and regex options, guarded by read-time hashes. Right-click files to preview, create, rename, delete, copy paths to chat drafts, or reveal in the system file manager.

file-gateway.description: Browse files across your VesnALIA machines and FTP/SFTP sites, then add the right file to a chat. Preview folders and media, download individual files or a folder’s visible files as a ZIP, and insert native file mentions without exposing account passwords to agents. Requires connected VesnALIA machines or reachable website accounts; macOS/Linux, read-only website access, 256 MiB between VesnALIA hosts and 32 MiB from websites. English interface with drag-to-chat mentions and hidden-file controls.

file-manager.description: Manage the files on the machine VesnALIA runs on without a terminal: browse, upload, move, rename, extract and hand them to the agent. Opens as a sidebar page, as a tab beside a thread that can start in that thread's folder, and from a file link in a message. Double-click shows images, PDF, video, Markdown and code; Space looks inside zip, tar, 7z and rar archives without extracting them. Multi-gigabyte uploads resume after a dropped connection, and several files or a whole folder download as one zip. On a phone, selected rows get an Actions bar with the whole row menu. Access stays inside the home folder of the user VesnALIA runs as; tar, 7z and rar archives need tar and 7z on that machine.

file-pins.description: Keep a thread's key files and links one click away, in a strip right above the composer. Each pin shows its file icon or site icon and is as wide as its label, with extra pins waiting in a ⋯ list. Type file names or URLs after the Pin pill and the agent finds and pins them; agents also pin the PR, issue, spec and dev server they work with on their own. Right-click a pin to preview, copy, unpin or remove it.

file-pretty.description: Read structured files with consistent formatting inside VesnALIA. Switch between formatted and raw content, and copy the view on screen. Parse errors show their location in the file. Supports JSON, JSON Lines, YAML, TOML, XML, and XML-based formats. Formatting TOML omits comments; the raw view retains them.

file-tree.description: Keep project files in view while you move between VesnALIA threads. Pin a project source or thread workspace, search by name or path, and preview files. Send a file path to a chosen chat draft, create a blank markdown file, or delete a file after confirmation. Copy paths or files, and reveal files in Finder. Requires access to the files on the VesnALIA machine; Finder reveal is macOS-only.

file-versions.description: See which copy of a deck, document or spreadsheet is the latest across all your projects. Groups v2, final, dated and (1) copies of one document, in English and Russian. Copies in archive folders never count as the latest ahead of a current one. Agents get the same answer from VesnALIA file-versions list, so they work from the right file. Reads project folders on the VesnALIA server and never changes a file.

files.description: Browse and safely edit files in the current VesnALIA thread environment.

files-editor.description: A VS Code-style file explorer and editor for the workspace behind a thread. Search in files finds a word across every file in the project: results are grouped by file with each hit highlighted, and clicking one opens the file on that line. It is smart case, with match-case, whole-word and regex toggles, and built for typing — file contents stay in memory between searches, so refining a query re-runs in tens of milliseconds, and a regex runs in its own worker so a runaway pattern cannot freeze VesnALIA. Around it: a file tree that shows dotfiles, editor tabs, a go-to-file palette (Cmd+P), find in the open file (Cmd+F), syntax highlighting in your VesnALIA code theme, and edit and save guarded so a change an agent made underneath you is never clobbered. Markdown files open rendered, with the source and the editor one click away. Two pickers choose the project and then its checkout or one of its worktrees; beside a thread it is pinned to that thread's worktree. Adds a `alia files` command so agents can browse and read the same workspace from the CLI, on whichever machine it lives.

finder.description: Browse, edit, and review the files an agent is working on without leaving VesnALIA. Every changed file carries a git status letter in the tree, and one click opens its diff, unified or side by side. An outline panel lists every class, function, and heading in the open file and puts the caret on the one you click. The CodeMirror editor saves with compare-and-swap, so a change the agent made while you were typing stops the save instead of overwriting it. Search in files reads every file in the workspace and opens a hit at its line, an @ mention attaches a file, or the lines you selected, resolved at send time, and markdown renders Mermaid diagrams. A workspace on another machine works the same way.

firstmate.description: Turn one thread into a crew: dispatch parallel agent ships in their own worktrees and land their work when it reports DONE. Ships get isolated git worktrees, scouts stay read-only, and every crew ends with a DONE, BLOCKED, or FAILED verdict. Thread events ping you the moment a crew finishes, fails, or stalls, and a crew that idles without a verdict gets nudged until it reports. Queue work with dependencies, gate merges behind green checks, and hand whole projects to domain captains. Requires the VesnALIA CLI on the host; the optional real firstmate toolbelt clones upstream firstmate scripts.

firstmate-crew.description: Hand one agent your to-do list and it runs a crew of worker threads, each in its own git worktree, until the work lands. The first mate is a pinned thread in VesnALIA's own chat that writes each worker's instructions, supervises it, and brings back branches, pull requests, findings and only the decisions that are yours. A FirstMate tab shows the crew as a board of Queued, Working, Blocked, Parked, Done, Failed and Idle, with Steer, Interrupt, Relaunch and End on every card. A built-in watch tells the first mate within about five minutes when a pull request is merged, reviewed or changes check status. Requires VesnALIA 0.47 or later, git, and the logged-in gh CLI for the pull request watch; a capable model such as Claude Sonnet is recommended for the first mate.

flare.description: Let an agent tell you what it found while it is still working, not only in the message that ends its turn. Agents get a `flare` tool and send a finding, a decision, a progress or status update, a blocker or a summary; the newest one shows in a banner above the message box, and the thread's Flares tab keeps them all, drawn the way VesnALIA draws a reply, so an agent can answer with a chart, a diagram, a table or a snippet instead of describing it. Blockers, and flares the agent marks urgent, send a push notification, so alerts reach you while the work carries on. A child thread's flares appear in its parent's tab, and a child's blocker reaches the parent's agent as a note without starting a turn. The tool returns at once, so the agent never waits, and `alia flare send` works from a terminal or another agent.

flexible-worktrees.description: Turns a pull request, branch, or new task into a ready worktree for the thread, with no Git commands to type. One picker searches open PRs, local and remote branches, and existing checkouts, then says exactly what launching will do. New branches start from the freshly fetched default branch, and PRs, including ones from forks, open as detached review worktrees. Worktrees go where your path template puts them, get their submodules and .worktreeinclude files, and are never deleted. Requires VesnALIA 0.43+ and Git 2.31+ on the selected machine; the GitHub CLI is optional, for listing PRs.

flexoki.description: Read and write on warm paper and ink with Flexoki by Steph Ango (kepano/flexoki): light and dark palettes, syntax and terminal colours.

floating-notes.description: Keep a note beside the work it belongs to, one keystroke from any thread. Notes group themselves by project, thread and day, so nothing lands in a flat pile. Stickies pin to a thread or a project and appear only while you are looking at it, and every thread gets a scratchpad your agents can append findings to. Writes real markdown — clickable checklists, highlighted code fences, wiki links — and stores everything in a local SQLite file with no account and no network.

floating-terminal.description: Adds a draggable terminal window over VesnALIA, opened from the sidebar footer or Ctrl+`, with a tab per shell in any project checkout or machine home directory; tabs are persisted, so a reload or a VesnALIA restart reattaches to the same shells with their scrollback.

focus-board.description: A kanban of your VesnALIA threads, focused on what needs you first. Group threads by attention, last activity, project, provider, machine, or parent; drag to act — hand-order a column, change a card's state in the drag, or nest a child; sweep stale lanes, snooze threads, and search titles, projects, and branches. Cards show state, pin, pending-interaction badge, update time, and branch or host; a click opens the thread and a modified click opens it in a new window.

focus-mode.description: Read a conversation as plain text, with tool calls, file edits, and every panel out of sight. Your prompts appear as quiet quotes and the agent's replies in one narrow column, refreshed every two seconds while the agent works. A small dot shows when the agent is running, and older history loads on request. Open it from the thread header or command palette, assign a shortcut in VesnALIA's Keyboard settings, and press Escape to return to your unchanged layout and draft.

focus-sidebar.description: Keeps only the threads from the last few hours in your sidebar and moves older ones to an Archive grouped by day. Threads that are running, waiting for your answer or pinned stay in Focus whatever their age, and you pick the window: 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 hours. A search box matches titles, projects and branches as you type, then message text across open and closed threads. Every row and the thread header get a close button that uses VesnALIA's own archive with Undo; nothing is archived automatically.

followups.description: Turn a finished answer into your next message: pick one of its suggested follow-ups and get a full draft in the composer. When a thread finishes, a model reads its last answer and your last three messages, then shows two to five next steps above the message box, each with the reason it is worth doing. Click one, or press 1–9, and it is written out as a first-person message in your composer; nothing is sent for you, and anything you typed stays. A switch in each thread's header turns follow-ups on or off for that thread, and a footer shows how long each run took and how many tokens it used. Each suggestion and draft is a short run on a model you choose from your VesnALIA providers, in a hidden worker thread that uses the provider's least privileged permission mode and is deleted when it finishes.

fonts.description: Choose local font families and tune interface, code, and serif typography independently of VesnALIA's active theme. Each role inherits size, weight, style, line height, and letter spacing from the theme until you override it, with live specimens before you save. Search the fonts installed on the device you view VesnALIA from, or type any family name. Installed-font discovery needs a secure desktop Chromium context; generic and manually entered families work everywhere, and no font data leaves the client.

forage.description: Put web research in every agent's hands and keep what it found in a per-thread Research tab you can read, quote and cite. web_search, web_fetch, web_map, web_extract, web_crawl and web_diff run as VesnALIA's own tools for every provider, with routing profiles, domain and date filters, bounded limits and every partial failure in words. Replies carry citation cards that quote the exact kept lines a claim rests on, and Check in sources matches any message against the pages stored for that thread. A zero-turn CLI runs the same operations; private networks are blocked by default and keyless DuckDuckGo and Exa search need no account.

fx.description: Run the fx coding agent in VesnALIA threads. Pick models available to your account, follow replies and tool activity, and resume sessions. Requires the fx CLI and an authenticated fx account; model access and charges depend on your provider.

genui.description: Turns agent replies into charts, diagrams, maps, plans and forms you can use, right in the chat. Agents choose from 86 components on their own, with no setup: sliders and filters recompute in the page, and buttons, choices and forms put your answers in your message, which reaches the agent when you send it. Test reports, logs, lint errors and coverage files render as their own components instead of pasted text, and a thread's changes, commits, pull request and workers are read live from VesnALIA. Adds about 6,400 tokens of instructions to sessions whose replies you read, and looks up photos, places and map tiles on Wikimedia Commons, Wikipedia, Photon and OpenStreetMap unless you turn web lookups off. Relies on VesnALIA internals, so a VesnALIA update can show the blocks as code until the plugin catches up.

gh-copilot.description: Registers GitHub Copilot CLI as the acp-gh-copilot provider in VesnALIA.

gh-projects-board.description: See what you are actually working on, in the columns your team already agreed on. The board reads the Status field of a GitHub Projects v2 board, so Todo, In Progress and QA arrive in the project's own order with each option's description, instead of every assigned issue landing in one pile. A My Tasks filter opens on your own unfinished work, and GitHub's filter syntax works as it does on github.com, including assignee:@me and negation. Group by any single-select field, not only Status. Requires the GitHub CLI signed in on the machine running the VesnALIA server, with a classic token carrying the read:project scope, because fine-grained tokens cannot read user-owned projects.

gh-stack.description: Visualizes and drives stacked pull requests from a VesnALIA thread panel, wrapping the gh stack CLI for split, push, submit, and merge.

ghostrunner.description: Turn VesnALIA into a cyberpunk console with near-black panels, a hot red accent, cyan for success and diffs, and yellow for warnings. Text uses JetBrains Mono and titles Chakra Petch, with a monospace fallback, and code previews get matching syntax colours. Dark only. No wallpapers are bundled: the overview links some that suit the theme, which you can set with Aura.

gigaam.description: Dictate in Russian with the VesnALIA microphone and get punctuated text, recognized on your own machine. On first load the plugin installs GigaAM v3, Sber's open Russian speech model, with a private Python and CPU-only PyTorch, so nothing is set up by hand. A 10-second phrase takes about 1 second on a 10-core CPU, and recordings over 20 seconds are split at pauses, so minute-long voice notes work. Audio never leaves the machine, or you can point the plugin at your own OpenAI-compatible transcription server. Needs Linux (x86-64 or arm64) or macOS on Apple silicon, about 2 GB of disk, 1.5 GB of RAM, and a one-time 1.2 GB download; recognizes Russian only.

git-graph.description: Follow branches, merges, and commit history beside your VesnALIA thread. Browse up to 200 commits with branch and tag labels, switch between configured repositories, and inspect history from the CLI. Runs Git in the thread's local or connected remote environment without changing the repository. Requires VesnALIA 0.47.1+, Git in the environment, and npm for installation; no external account or paid service is needed.

git-history.description: Shows the complete Git history of a project as a compact commit graph with changed files and per-file diffs.

git-panel.description: Git for the thread's workspace: stage, AI-commit, branch, and sync without leaving VesnALIA.

git-worktrees.description: Pick any existing git worktree for a project and start a thread there in one click. Lists paths from git worktree list on the selected machine, excluding ALIA-managed worktrees. Attaches the picked path with ownsPath: false, so VesnALIA never deletes it when the thread retires. Requires a project checkout and Git on the selected machine.

gitea.description: Manage Gitea issues and pull requests from VesnALIA. Review diffs, discuss changes, and handle labels, assignments, and status from a thread panel or the VesnALIA gitea command. Turn on Auto-fix or Auto-merge from My PRs or Pull requests. Install the tea CLI and sign in to your Gitea instance; agent actions use your configured VesnALIA model and tea permissions.

github-actions.description: Watch every GitHub Actions run of your VesnALIA projects, start any workflow with its inputs, and hand failures to an agent. A failed job opens its log at the error line, and Ask agent starts a thread with that excerpt and a brief to find the root cause. Run workflow turns a workflow_dispatch trigger into a form with branch, choice, and boolean inputs, checked before the request reaches GitHub. Rerun failed jobs, cancel a run, or send a run report to the VesnALIA threads you pick and subscribe them to new failures. Requires a GitHub account: the plugin uses the gh CLI login on the VesnALIA server machine, or a token you set.

github-app-auth.description: Run your VesnALIA agents as a GitHub App, so pull requests and commits open under the app's name and you can review them on GitHub. Each agent turn gets a short-lived installation token as GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN, so gh and git act as the app. Commits use the app's bot identity and pushes go over the token. Enable only the projects you choose, with the scopes you grant the app, and personal projects stay yours. Needs a GitHub App you create and the gh CLI on the machines that run threads.

github-board.description: See your GitHub issues, pull requests and discussions on one board, and hand any of them to an agent thread. Four columns cover what you wrote, what is open on repositories you own and what is assigned to you, and an issue that a pull request closes folds into that pull request's card. Pull request cards show CI checks and branch status, with an Update branch button wherever you can push. A detail panel shows the body, comments and images, and labels are added or removed from a right-click menu. Send to chat opens VesnALIA's new-thread composer on a card, with a prompt you set per column and per project, in the VesnALIA project that has the repository checked out. Add to chat puts the same prompt, the card's column template with the chat's project override, at the end of a chat's draft without sending it, from a menu of the chats on screen and your recent threads. Requires VesnALIA 0.47 or later, and the GitHub CLI (gh) installed and signed in on the machine running the VesnALIA server.

github-extended.description: Browses cached GitHub issues, pull requests, and Dependabot alerts in VesnALIA with thread actions and agent-assisted work.

github-folder.description: The open GitHub pull requests that need you, as a folder at the top of the sidebar: review requests, then your own PRs with changes requested, failing checks or conflicts, and the ones ready to merge. Click a PR to start a thread with its title, status, branch and description as context, in the project whose remote is that repository. Snooze a PR until it changes, and pick sources, drafts and organizations. Reads GitHub through the gh CLI on the VesnALIA server; Thread Tree draws the folder in its own list when installed.

github-pr-dashboard.description: See why each pull request is stuck, and get it unstuck, without leaving VesnALIA. My PRs lists your pull requests, review requests for you and your teams, the ones you reviewed, and assigned ones by repository, each with its +/- lines and led by what blocks it: failing CI down to the job, changes requested, unresolved comments, conflicts or a stack. Reviewed turns amber when the author pushes after your review. Open one for its reviewers and their verdicts, labels, and tabs: Overview (the description, then comments and reviews), Checks with error annotations, Files with syntax-highlighted diffs and review threads under their lines, Commits with the ones since your review marked, and Comments. Edit the title and description, comment on a line or range, reply, delete your own comments, submit a review, mark your draft ready, and close or reopen, each only when you click. A menu links the PR to a VesnALIA thread, asks about it, explains it, or sends every finding to an agent, starting in the PR's project; Fix with agent does it for one comment or failed job. Jira keys open in VesnALIA's My Jira plugin. Search, hide or fold repositories, move by keyboard, switch gh accounts, and get alerts when CI fails or someone comments. Uses the GitHub CLI login or a token; github.com only.

github-projects.description: Creates and imports GitHub repositories directly from VesnALIA's native project picker. Injects dedicated creation and import options into the project dropdown. Automatically initializes private repositories, clones locally, and registers projects in VesnALIA with one click. Also provides the VesnALIA gh-project CLI and agent skill.

gitlab.description: Browses GitLab issues and merge requests in a VesnALIA panel, with pipelines, approvals, discussions and diffs, and spawns an agent thread on any of them.

gitlab-interface-notion-style.description: Review, merge and fix GitLab merge requests without leaving VesnALIA. Each merge request opens on a readiness strip that names what blocks it, and counts approvals and 👍 reactions as review. Reply to and resolve threads, read a failed job's log and retry it, or start a pipeline on any branch. Requires the glab CLI logged in to your GitLab host.

glass.description: Translucent VesnALIA surfaces with six animated backdrops, custom GLSL shaders, wallpaper, and adjustable frost. Preview your look and tune colors, surfaces, and motion.

goals.description: Keep your personal priorities available when you ask an agent to evaluate an idea or plan. Reorder goals and archive completed ones. Goals do not launch work automatically. Agent evaluations use your configured provider quota.

gone-fishing.description: Turn the wait for your agent into a pixel-art fishing trip on top of the chat input. The pond fishes by itself while a turn runs, or you take the rod to hook, reel, and land each fish yourself. Water floods the chat input behind your text, and the fish swimming there are the ones that bite. Three maps hold 28 species, and the seasons follow your calendar. Your catches unlock new maps and gear for your angler, boat, and dog. Catches stay in a local database on the VesnALIA server and use no external service.

google-antigravity-acp.description: Adds Google Antigravity as a VesnALIA agent provider through its official ACP server (agy_acp_server.par), with the same provider bridge as VesnALIA's built-in ACP agents.

graph-studio.description: Build agent loops that go back when review fails, run them on real VesnALIA threads, and watch every step live. A node spawns a thread rather than calling a model, so workers appear in the sidebar and run on the providers you already have. Describe a flow in the chat and the agent builds and starts it, or open the studio from the command palette; the run shows up as a live card in the thread. 31 templates, human and dialogue nodes, per-attempt token counts, checkpointed runs. The work templates use Matt Pocock's skills, a separate install (npx skills add mattpocock/skills).

graphite-mono.description: Set VesnALIA in JetBrains Mono at Light weight with a compact reading scale and a rounded composer, in Graphite and Matrix palettes.
graphite-mono.licenseNote: в package.json указано "MIT", в репозитории permission

graphite-stack.description: Review stacked changes alongside your VesnALIA threads. Inspect parent-relative diffs and keep local comments before sending them to a linked thread. Review GitHub pull requests and preview stack actions. Requires the Graphite CLI; GitHub review features also require an authenticated GitHub CLI.

grok-build-usage.description: Adds live Grok Build subscription and weekly credit usage, including reset timing, to VesnALIA's Settings → Usage Limits page.

gtd-sidebar.description: Replaces the VesnALIA thread list with an inbox that splits threads into Next Action and Waiting, and clears them with snooze and settle.

guest-view.description: Share one thread with someone who has no VesnALIA account: they follow it live in a browser and suggest prompts that you approve. Guests see your messages and the agent's replies as they happen, with tool work shown only as counts such as "Ran 3 commands, edited 2 files". Each suggestion waits in a card above your composer, where you choose Use, Copy or Dismiss, so nothing a guest writes reaches the agent until you send it. The card also shows who is connected, kicks a guest, ends the link, and sets how long it lasts (4 hours by default). The link is a free Cloudflare quick tunnel, so the thread's text passes through Cloudflare and anyone with the link can watch; it needs the separate cloudflared program (on Linux the plugin can download a pinned, checksummed copy when you ask), and it requires VesnALIA 0.48 or later.

guided-review.description: Organizes GitHub pull requests into chapters, with code diffs, private notes, a contextual assistant, and review feedback you edit and submit.

handoff.description: Moves a whole session between agents and machines in both directions: hands a VesnALIA thread's rendered transcript to another provider (optionally on another enrolled machine, carrying uncommitted work as a patch), or adopts a Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or OpenCode session from your terminal as a VesnALIA thread in the same directory.

hands-free.description: Talk to VesnALIA threads on iPhone and hear replies in Microsoft Edge neural voices. Choose a thread, dictate, and send with a tap; speech is sent without review. Requires microphone access and configured voice transcription; spoken replies send text to Microsoft. No Read Aloud installation is needed.

handsfree.description: Adds a hands-free voice operator to VesnALIA: talk to an agent that focuses threads, sends messages, starts work, and shows diffs.

harness.description: Adds an opt-in Explore, Plan, Worker, Critic, and Promote workflow to VesnALIA threads with explicit DAGs, role routing, audit artifacts, and custom Harness definitions.

hashstash.description: Reuse saved prompts in any VesnALIA chat and edit them before sending. Type # to search by name and insert a template. Keep your library as Markdown files in a folder you choose. No external service or API key is required.

hats.description: Workspaces for your VesnALIA sidebar: switch between groups of projects, like Work and Personal, with one click. Each hat is a workspace that holds a set of projects, and a project can sit in several hats. A footer button switches to the next hat: projects that other hats claim are hidden, and projects in no hat always show. Your sidebar order, threads, and collapsed groups stay exactly as you left them. Edit hats and pick their icons on the settings page, or use the VesnALIA hats CLI; no account or external service.

haze.description: Puts your own image behind every VesnALIA conversation as a soft haze that fades out before the text. Pick one of six effects (None, Dither, ASCII, Halftone, Scanlines, Haze) and set a separate background for each project. Window glass can blur the same image behind the whole window, with a see-through sidebar and main pane. Images stay in your VesnALIA server's local database; no account is needed. Turn off Aura while Haze is on.

header-pins.description: Switch between your pinned threads in one click from the empty title bar strip at the top of the VesnALIA window. Each chip carries a status dot for the thread and its child threads: yellow waits for you, blue works, green finished and unread. A colored bar marks the thread with its project color when Chat Sidebar by Evgeniy Perin is installed, which we recommend, and with its provider's color otherwise. Hover a chip to unpin it in place. Needs the VesnALIA desktop app; no account or network access.

headroom.description: Context budget monitoring — tells agents how much of the model's context window is used (real usage events, not estimates) and when to summarise or start fresh.

herald.description: Hear one spoken sentence when an agent needs you, and see every waiting thread in one list. When a thread asks a question, waits for a plan or a permission to be approved, finishes its turn or fails, the VesnALIA app says which thread it is and what it needs, on whatever page you are on. A Herald page in the sidebar lists every thread waiting on you with its reason and sentence, and the same sentence sits above that thread's composer with a Read again button until you answer. Settings choose which kinds of event are announced, the voice and speed, and where to speak: the desktop app, a browser tab, or the mobile app while it is open. By default the sentence is built from the event itself, with no model or external service; optionally, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI or a command of your own, installed and logged in on the Mac running VesnALIA, writes it instead, for one short model turn per announcement. The default voice needs VesnALIA running on a Mac, and elsewhere each device's own browser voice speaks. Requires VesnALIA 0.47 or later.

herdr-theme.description: Turn VesnALIA into a terminal-style workspace, with framed conversation panes and eleven color palettes in light and dark. Child threads hang from their parent as a connected tree in the sidebar. Turn on branch names to show each project thread's Git branch beneath its title. JetBrains Mono ships inside the plugin, so no font service, account, or API key is needed. Requires VesnALIA 0.43 or later.

hex.description: On-device voice dictation for VesnALIA's chat composer and `alia voice transcribe`, powered by Hex and macOS 26's built-in Apple Speech (SpeechTranscriber + SpeechAnalyzer) or local GGUF speech models (Parakeet, Whisper, Qwen3-ASR, Cohere Transcribe, Nemotron). Starts a warm embedded `hex service --embedded` daemon when VesnALIA loads the plugin, adds a Voice Provider picker directly to the composer microphone right-click menu, transcodes browser microphone clips (`audio/webm`, `audio/mp4`, `audio/ogg`) to 16 kHz mono PCM WAV via `ffmpeg`, and stops the daemon automatically when VesnALIA exits.

higgsfield.description: Shows how many Higgsfield credits you have, when they reset, and how many will expire unused at your current pace. A burn forecast charts this cycle's balance and projects it to the reset date, so you see whether you run out early or leave credits behind. A per-model table counts generations, refunded failures, credits, and cost per generation, tagged image, video, audio, or text. A daily chart stacks spend by model or media type for this cycle, 7, 30, or 90 days. Requires the Higgsfield CLI and a Higgsfield account; sign-in uses Higgsfield's own browser login.

hmm-floating-terminal.description: Keep a shell open beside the project you are working in, without leaving the conversation for a panel or another app. The window follows the project: leave for another one and it steps aside, come back and its tabs return with the dev server still running. Shells belong to the project checkout rather than to a thread, so moving between a project's threads never costs you one. Sessions belong to VesnALIA, so closing the window leaves a build or an ssh session running and reopening replays the scrollback. Drag the grip to resize, minimize to the title bar, or maximize to fill the app. Requires VesnALIA 0.42 or newer and Plugin SDK 0.4.47 or newer.

home-hero.description: Greets you on VesnALIA's home screen with the time of day and, when you set one, your name. Optionally upload a PNG, JPEG or WebP icon up to 256 KiB; it travels over VesnALIA's existing plugin connection and is stored with the plugin on the VesnALIA server, never in the repository. Without a name or icon the greeting is plain text. Requires VesnALIA 0.49.0+.

homepage.description: Starts new chats from configurable homepage project cards with manual sorting, pinning, renaming, hiding, activity sparklines, and artwork.

hooks.description: Run your own commands and webhooks when VesnALIA threads change state, and hold each outgoing message to your own policy. Install notification, integration, automation and guard templates from the marketplace catalog, each rated for performance and security, or write hooks by hand. React to thread lifecycle events with filters on project, provider, title and text; gate hooks proceed, reject with a reason, or wait before dispatch. Secrets stay AES-256-GCM encrypted and are referenced without storing values in hook definitions; manage everything from the Hooks page, `alia hooks`, or the bundled agent skills. Commands run on the machine hosting the VesnALIA server with the server user's access.

host-monitor.description: Monitors CPU, memory, disk, network throughput, load, uptime, and user-owned processes across every machine enrolled in VesnALIA, with guarded controls to stop eligible processes.

host-pulse.description: Keep server load, provider quotas, reset countdowns, and DeepSeek balance in view while you work in VesnALIA. Pin a draggable card with per-core CPU, disk busy time and IOPS, network speed, and CPU/RAM process leaders; detailed activity needs Linux. Quotas use VesnALIA's Provider usage plugin and configured accounts; the optional balance row needs local DSH with a DeepSeek API key and calls DeepSeek's balance API. Open charts and diagnostics, or enable background CPU and memory alerts.

hotspot.description: Names the VesnALIA thread that is making your Mac hot, and lets you stop the dev server or build behind it. A flame in the sidebar footer shows CPU and memory every 2 seconds; click it for the busiest threads, each thread's processes, and a kill that lists what it stops and what it spares before it runs. The Hotspot page keeps seven days of per-minute CPU, memory and thermal history, shades each hot spell, and ranks the threads that caused it. Agents answer "why was my Mac hot at 3pm?" with a built-in tool, and the VesnALIA hotspot command answers it in a terminal. Built for macOS, with no account or network service; on Linux it tracks CPU, memory and threads but has no thermal reading, and Windows is not supported.

human-tasks.description: Collect the steps only you can do in one checklist, and the agent that asked resumes when you finish. Agents hand you tasks with steps, like creating an API key, adding a DNS record, or testing a build on your phone, each linked to the project, thread, and bot that asked. Each task says what the agent would need to do it itself, such as an MCP server, an API key, or your browser, so you can do it or let the agent do it. Blocking tasks wait as a form in their thread so your push notifications fire, and credentials come back through VesnALIA's secret form instead of the chat.

image-diff.description: See exactly which pixels changed in an image before you approve it. Before, Diff and After sit side by side, with changed pixels highlighted over a white background, over the new image, or blinking, plus a changed-pixel count. Git LFS images render in place in VesnALIA's Diff tab, downloading missing objects on demand. A pinned Image diff tab lists every changed image in the thread, and opening a changed image anywhere shows its diff. LFS images need git-lfs on the host.

image-preview.description: Adds responsive image grids and a click-to-expand gallery to VesnALIA chat messages.

image-studio.description: Keep generated project photos in a gallery and create or edit the next image from the panel or chat. People profiles use labeled reference sheets and can build missing face, body, and detail views for reuse across models. Nano Banana 2, 2.1, Pro, and Muse Image use paid fal.ai or kie.ai API keys; Muse Image requires fal.ai. The chat Send form remembers the model, frame, and size, with 2K as the default size; the interface supports English and Russian, and Env Catalog can hold the keys.

impromptu-ui.description: Turn your agent's walls of text into interfaces you can click. Triage a milestone from rows that each carry a drafted comment and Post and close, Post, and Start thread buttons. Split one review comment into several pull requests, each waiting on its own card with its diff until you click Commit, push, and open PR. Find a design by picking from screenshots of the original and its variations, with a note on each. Requires VesnALIA 0.43 or later, and needs no account or external service.

inbox.description: Questions, failed runs, finished threads, and extension activity in one inbox, with dismissible popups, optional Telegram alerts, and guided setup.

inline-comments.description: Comment on exact passages of an agent's reply and send every comment with your next message. Select text, choose Add to chat, and type or dictate a note in a card next to the passage. Each passage stays highlighted and appears as a pill in the composer, where a click edits or deletes its comment. The agent receives each quoted passage next to its comment. Comments stay on your VesnALIA server; no external service or account is needed. Requires VesnALIA 0.46 or later.

inline-review.description: Turn passages from an assistant response into one clear revision request. Mark comments and removals while you read, keep them highlighted across navigation, add overall feedback, and send the full review to the same thread. Drafts stay on your VesnALIA server; no external service or account is required. Requires VesnALIA 0.43.x.

inline-terminal.description: Run the commands an agent suggests right under its reply, and have the agent read the result and answer on its own. Every bash, sh, zsh or console code block in a reply gets a Run button that opens a live terminal beneath it, where you can answer prompts, type passwords and press Ctrl-C. When the block finishes, its exit code and output reach the agent as hidden context, so it replies without you pasting anything and the chat gets no extra message. The shell starts in the thread's workspace with your startup files loaded and keeps cd, virtualenvs and variables for follow-up commands. Needs a macOS or Linux machine; no account or external service.

ios-simulator.description: Run and test mobile apps beside your VesnALIA thread, using the same screen as your agent. Capture up to the last 30 seconds of iOS video with input, app-log, and matching crash events. Hand control explicitly between you and your agent, with one controlling thread per device. Requires VesnALIA 0.46+, an Apple Silicon Mac with Xcode’s iOS platform and Node.js 20+ for iOS; Android screenshot previews need an installed SDK and AVD.

iris.description: Turns agent replies into live cards you can use: charts, test runs, decisions, plans, agent traces, eval reports and small apps, drawn in your VesnALIA theme. Agents pick from well over a hundred components on their own and check each card before you see it, so a status report arrives as metrics and progress, and proof of done as criteria with their evidence. Sliders and toggles recompute cards in place, buttons and pickers send your answer back to the agent (design variants, a theme preview, colors, marks on a screenshot, comments on a spec, a ranked list), and live cards re-read files while a job runs. Pin up to five live cards per thread, or let the agent pin a status card: a pinned chip above the composer opens them, VesnALIA's home page shows every thread's pins, and a pin can alert you when its condition turns true. Copy any card as an image, or open it in the web playground. Cards also read VesnALIA itself: the thread's context use, the threads it started, its pull request, commits, terminals and plan usage. Adds under 4,000 tokens of instructions to each top-level session, and maps and photos call OpenStreetMap, Photon and Wikimedia Commons unless you turn web lookups off.

jb-flow.description: Puts the agent threads that need you at the top, and keeps the rest out of the way until they do. A Triage sidebar ranks what to do next in Now: what's blocked on you, threads you mark as Focus, and deadlines coming up, above numbered lanes you move between with one key. Workspace tabs group projects, threads and tools by area of work. ⌘K searches threads, messages and PRs, and Tab on a result replies to it, snoozes, moves or archives it. Agents call wait_for_ci and end their turn instead of polling GitHub, and are messaged when checks finish or a review arrives. PR and CI features need the GitHub CLI.

jetbrains-central.description: Use work AI subscriptions alongside personal accounts and see shared JetBrains Central credits in VesnALIA. This is an unofficial plugin developed independently by an enthusiast. It is not an official JetBrains product. JetBrains Air is JetBrains' platform for coding agents and team AI access; this plugin connects VesnALIA through JetBrains Central CLI using your JetBrains Account. Choose separate Codex, Claude Code, and Pi providers, or configure additional ACP profiles. Requires VesnALIA 0.48+ with Plugin SDK 0.6.104+, Git, Node.js, Central with a work subscription or organization-provided AI access, and the corresponding agent CLIs; tested on macOS.

jev-please-proceed.description: Keep agents moving when they stop only to ask for an unnecessary confirmation. Jev reviews the complete available top-level conversation whenever a thread becomes idle and continues only when its Noul value exceeds 0.95. Before sending `please proceed`, it confirms that the thread is still idle and has no pending interaction or queued message, then stops if the same final response repeats. Use a TypeSafe, Vercel AI Gateway, or OpenRouter API key; conversation text is sent through the selected provider for TypeSafe processing, and usage charges may apply.

jira.description: Browse, edit, and move Jira Cloud issues without leaving VesnALIA, and let agents change Jira only after you approve. Switch between a grouped list and a status board, and drag a card to move an issue through its workflow. Agents can search, create, edit, transition, comment on, assign, and delete issues, and each kind of change asks first unless you set it to always allow. Link a VesnALIA project to its Jira projects so that project's chats search only those issues, and Send to agent opens the chat in the linked project. Requires a Jira Cloud site and an Atlassian API token; Jira Server and Data Center are not supported.

jira-boards.description: Browse your Jira boards beside the chat and add any ticket's current context to your next message. Columns, quick filters, JQL and swimlanes by assignee, epic or priority keep the board to the work you care about, and the tab reopens on your last board and filters. Drag a card into the composer or press Add to chat, and VesnALIA fetches the issue, its fields and newest comments when you send. Agents can read issues, individual fields, comment pages, text attachments such as logs and JSON, and linked issues and subtasks in one call, and post a comment, move a ticket through its workflow or assign it to you when you ask, as your own Jira account. Works with Jira Data Center or Server through a personal access token and with Jira Cloud through an API token plus account email; the VesnALIA server needs HTTPS access to the Jira site. Needs VesnALIA 0.47 or newer.

jira-dc.description: Browse and update Jira Data Center issues from VesnALIA, and let agents change them only after you approve. Open a list or status board, edit fields in place, and drag a card through the workflow. Agents can search, create, edit, transition, comment on, assign, and delete issues, with each write kind asking first unless you set it to always allow. Link a VesnALIA project to its Jira projects so chats stay scoped, spawn a thread from an issue, or drive the same actions with VesnALIA jira-dc. Requires a reachable Jira Data Center (or Server) base URL and a Personal Access Token; Jira Cloud is not supported.

kata.description: Track and triage kata issues from the keyboard, beside the VesnALIA thread doing the work. One tab per kata project puts the issue list and the issue detail side by side, updated live from the kata daemon. Press n for a new issue inline, N for a child of the selection, and !0-!4 to set priority without leaving the list. A thread whose checkout holds a .kata.toml gets a Kata issues side panel, clickable issue chips in messages, and kata_* tools its agent can call. The VesnALIA kata CLI covers the same ground from any VesnALIA terminal. Requires kata installed on the same machine with its daemon running; no account, token, or hosted service.

keep-last-blocks-open.description: Keeps the newest work blocks open while the agent works, so the output stays in view without clicks. Blocks count at every depth, so the commands inside a group count toward the limit. After the final answer only the last block stays open. Settings set the running count from 0 to 10, the count after the answer from 0 to 3, and whether Thought rows count. Needs no account or external service.

kernel-browser.description: Open, watch, and drive KERNEL cloud browsers from VesnALIA threads and the VesnALIA CLI.

kilocode.description: First-class Kilo Code provider for VesnALIA.

kimi-code.description: Adds Moonshot's Kimi Code as a provider: run its threads from VesnALIA's provider picker, locally and on enrolled remote hosts. Turns stream into the native VesnALIA timeline — replies and tool calls such as file edits and shell commands — with resume and VesnALIA permission modes gating each action. The model picker fills from Kimi Code itself (K3, K3-256k, K2.8 Preview, K2.7 Code Highspeed), with thinking levels and the Default / Plan / Auto / YOLO mode selector. Kimi Code's slash commands (/compact, /status, /usage, and your own skill commands) appear in the composer menu. Requires the Kimi Code CLI and a signed-in account on each host (kimi login); the provider card can install the CLI where it is missing.

kimi-quota.description: See Kimi Code quota beside Codex and Claude limits in one VesnALIA usage card. Shows the 5-hour window, monthly coding and total limits, with reset times; also provides the VesnALIA kimi-quota command. Uses Kimi's API and requires Kimi Code CLI installed and signed in on the VesnALIA server, plus a Kimi membership that includes Kimi Code.

kimi-usage.description: Shows the Kimi Code 5-hour and monthly limits in VesnALIA's usage panel, where no collector reads them. The panel covers the OpenCode Go and Claude Code subscriptions only, so a Kimi Code plan shows nothing; this adds the windows Kimi reports, with the percentage used and the reset time. The row appears only when the Kimi Code ACP provider is installed, and a host whose login expired drops out instead of leaving an empty row. Requires a Kimi Code subscription signed in on the host.

kodaforge.description: Edit, run and debug your project inside VesnALIA, with agent chat, threads and workflows open beside the code. A Monaco code editor with tabs, split editors, quick open (⌘P), find in files, and search and replace with a preview. Language servers (LSP) for Python and TypeScript give completion, go to definition, find references, rename and a Problems panel. Debug Python with breakpoints, pick the Python environment (venv, uv, Poetry, conda), run Makefile and npm tasks, and work in split terminals that survive restarts. Source control stages, diffs, commits, stashes, pulls and pushes with git. The Agent Network maps the agents and MCP servers working on your project, and in App mode the agents, tools, MCP servers, models and skills your code builds. Install the language servers (pyright or basedpyright, typescript-language-server) and debugpy yourself.

korey.description: Bring all your Korey connectors into your coding conversations in VesnALIA. Research across connected services and create or update Shortcut Stories. Continue the same private Korey conversation across coding harnesses and attach workspace files. Requires a Korey account, a personal access token, and configured connectors.

kujo.description: Give VesnALIA the paper-and-ink design of Kujo, with hard edges and quiet background signal. Switch between light and dark palettes with matching code, diffs and terminal colors. Departure Mono and Tabler icons carry the technical details. Requires VesnALIA 0.43; no external account or service.

lame-duck.description: Make a busy VesnALIA server ready for maintenance while keeping new sends queued. Pause sends while active turns finish, and watch the active-thread and held-send counts in the sidebar. Resume queued work after the server restarts. Agents can manage the same flow through the VesnALIA CLI.

launchd-jobs.description: Run shell commands on your Mac on a cron schedule or a fixed interval, as launchd jobs that keep running while VesnALIA is closed. Each job is a LaunchAgent plist that launchd owns, so a missed fire runs once when the Mac wakes and a disabled job stays disabled across reboots. A sidebar page shows each job's launchd status, its last twenty runs with duration and exit code, and the tail of its log, which you can follow live. Run now, Enable, Disable, Edit and Delete do the launchctl work for you, and commands run through your login shell with your terminal's PATH. The sidebar row counts failing jobs, and a picker switches between the Macs connected to VesnALIA. An optional push notification tells you when a job starts failing, once per failure; it needs VesnALIA 0.48.1 or later with Push notifications on. Requires VesnALIA 0.47 or later and macOS.

lavender.description: Give your workspace a lavender palette, from charcoal-violet nights to pale-lilac days. Match conversations, menus, code previews and diffs with coordinated light and dark colors. Follow your Light, Dark or System setting while keeping your layout and fonts. All theme assets ship locally; no external account is required.

learning-exercises.description: Get a short exercise on the code your agents just wrote, so you keep understanding what lands in your repository. After a commit, new files, a schema change or a merged pull request, one line above the composer offers a 10–15 minute exercise; offers are decided from VesnALIA's own data, not by a model, and are capped at three answered a day. Start runs the session in a side thread forked from yours, where each question is a card for your answer and how sure you are, and the agent's turn ends while the card is open, so it cannot hint. A Learning tab in every thread's side panel shows the session in progress, starts an exercise on the last commit, the new files or a topic you type, and keeps the project's paused and earlier sessions with your answers. A session runs on the thread's own agent and uses its tokens; answers are stored on the machine running VesnALIA. Exercises adapted from Dr. Cat Hicks's Learning Opportunities (CC BY 4.0), not affiliated with or endorsed by the author. Requires VesnALIA 0.48.1 or later with VesnALIA's bundled Git plugin on; pull request offers also need GitHub PR Status.

lego.description: Split a coding task across parallel agents and get it back assembled and verified by one Master Builder, while a Lego model builds live. The planning agent writes an instruction book: bags that each own their files, the interfaces every bag must honour, and the steps to assemble them. You choose how many builders run, up to eight, and which provider and model the builders and the Master Builder use; nothing starts until you submit. A banner above the composer and a side-panel workbench show minifigure builders placing bricks as each step lands, and finished models go on a collector's shelf. Builders and the Master Builder are ordinary VesnALIA threads on providers you already set up, so a build spends several agents' worth of tokens.

letta-agents.description: Resume your local Letta agents from the sidebar without losing their saved conversations. See agent activity and dispatched tasks beside each agent. Keep agent providers out of the model picker unless you enable them. Requires a separate local Letta Docker installation with the supported filesystem layout, Docker access, and the VesnALIA ACP adapter; the adapter uses npx to install its pinned Letta ACP package.

limits.description: A floating pill in the bottom-right corner shows how much of your coding-plan quota is left: Claude Code, Codex and Cursor through VesnALIA's own collectors, plus GLM (Z.AI) and Kimi Code fetched directly. One ring per limit window, follows the open thread's harness, inline per-provider refresh, a two-column popup with Refresh-all, and a manual mode that makes no background requests at all. Requires VesnALIA 0.46+.

linear.description: Linear inside VesnALIA — a list-first issue browser, inbox, and create dialog served from a local mirror, thirteen linear_* agent tools, a VesnALIA linear CLI, and every thread resolving which issue it works on, shown live in the header and side panel and injected into agent context.

linear-card.description: See which Linear issue each chat is about, right in the thread header. Click the chip for the full card with its description and images, then open, change, or unlink it. A chat with no card opens your assigned issues, grouped by state and searchable, so you can link one in two clicks. Branches named by Linear (eng-123-…) attach their issue on their own, and long titles get a short AI label. Requires a Linear personal API key; short labels use VesnALIA's Account Pooler.

link-hovercards.description: See a pull request's CI, review and merge state by hovering its link, without leaving the thread. Works on GitHub pull requests, GitHub issues and Linear issues anywhere in VesnALIA. On a phone, long-press a link to open its card. GitHub cards need the GitHub CLI signed in on your VesnALIA server; Linear cards need a personal Linear API key.

liquid-glass.description: Adds dark and light translucent themes over a configurable wallpaper layer, with adjustable glass effects and vibrant accent colors.

live-markdown.description: Edit Markdown right in the side panel, with formatting rendered as you type and saves that change only the characters you typed. Tables stay tables while you edit: click a cell to change its raw Markdown in place, Tab to the next cell, and Tab past the last one to add a row. Every save checks the file's hash first, so a file an agent changed while you typed asks you to keep your version or load the disk version instead of being overwritten. It becomes the opener for .md, .mdx and .markdown files on install unless you already chose one under Settings, and needs VesnALIA 0.43 or later with no account or external service.

lobu.description: Starts every thread with what earlier threads learned in your project and saves new learnings to Lobu memory. Agents search your personal workspace and a linked team workspace before working, supersede outdated memories in place, and run through native tools or VesnALIA lobu CLI commands across every agent provider. Each thread's Lobu memory panel shows what the agent started with, looked up, and saved, with undo, project pins, and one-click sharing to your team workspace. A Lobu page in VesnALIA's sidebar shows what agents saved in VesnALIA threads, searches all of Lobu, and surfaces the inbox plus the devices and connections that need attention. Built-in setup on the New thread screen installs the Lobu CLI via bun or npm and connects to a Lobu Cloud account or a local Lobu instance running on your machine.

lock-area.description: Keep reference panes in place while opening work beside them. Uses compatible native locks, or offers a version-checked initializer with backup and restore for VesnALIA 0.43.1. Initialization requires a clean supported VesnALIA source checkout, installed dependencies and pnpm.

loom.description: Hand a goal to agents and keep the decisions. A planner turns it into a spec with tickets, acceptance criteria, checks and a merge plan, and a separate agent reviews the spec before you approve it. Workers then build each ticket in its own git worktree, Loom runs your checks, and reviewers on another model approve the work or send findings back. Approved work merges into an integration branch you land as one pull request, or opens as one pull request per ticket that Loom follows through CI. A full-screen Loom page shows what needs you, the board, every attempt and review, the changes before they land, insights on how the project went and a timeline you can rewind.

mac-watch.description: Watch the Mac that runs VesnALIA — battery, heat, disk and sleep — from your phone. A macOS-style sidebar page shows CPU, memory pressure, disk, network and power draw with 1, 6 and 24 hour charts, plus the apps that hold the machine awake. Processor, SSD and battery temperatures, macOS thermal pressure, SMART status and kernel panics are read without sudo. Pushes cover only real trouble: battery under 20%, overheating, memory or disk running out, battery-controller faults and an unexpected reboot, with warnings held until morning during quiet hours. macOS on Apple Silicon only; alerts need the push-notifications plugin, sleep and shutdown add a one-time sudoers rule, and the interface is in Russian.

machine-load.description: Compare CPU, memory, GPU, network and disk load of all your VesnALIA machines on one shared timeline, with up to 7 days of history. Each machine gets a card with load average, swap, disk usage, disk IO, CPU temperature and every GPU, including Intel integrated graphics and Apple silicon, read without root. Agents check load before a heavy job with VesnALIA machine-load --json. A sidebar badge appears when any machine passes 80% CPU or RAM. Apple silicon temperature and power need macmon, installed separately.

machine-monitor.description: Check CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network and battery on any of your VesnALIA machines from one sidebar panel. Pick the VesnALIA server, your own machines or VesnALIA Box boxes from a searchable list, and each opens with live charts and its five busiest processes. On Apple silicon Macs it adds CPU and GPU temperature and power, read by a small bundled helper that needs no root. Tailscale name, address and tags sit at the bottom, each with a copy button. Works on Linux, macOS and WSL, and optional in-app alerts warn when the VesnALIA server stays overloaded.

machine-sidebar.description: Sort your VesnALIA threads by the machine they run on, then by project, so laptop and remote work never mix. Mark quiet threads or whole projects inactive to fold them into a dimmed group at the bottom; they come back when a turn finishes or waits for you. Start a title with [Tag] to show a colored pill, with a color per tag you pick in the plugin settings. Each row shows its git branch, a status dot, and icons for subagents or background commands; with farcall-mcp, worker tasks appear under their coordinator, each with the worktree it runs in.

machine-status.description: See battery charge, memory use, and disk use for every machine connected to VesnALIA in one sidebar list. Each metric turns red at a threshold you set — 20% battery, 90% memory or storage by default. The list refreshes only when a whole-percent value changes, so it stays still while you work. Turn off the metrics you do not need; everything comes from each machine's own OS interfaces, with no account or external service.

magic-compose.description: Choose where a new thread runs as you type your prompt. Let Jev select the project, machine, model, reasoning level, and environment, then review or override each choice before sending. Tune its choices with your instructions and try routing a prompt from settings. Requires VesnALIA 0.43+ and a Vercel AI Gateway or OpenRouter API key; prompts, routing instructions, project context, and machine information are sent to TypeSafe through your gateway, with usage charges.

magpie.description: Connect VesnALIA to a Magpie gateway and see what your agents cost. The Magpie page shows estimated cost, tokens over time per agent, cache hit rate, subscription allowance with reset times, and a breakdown by model, agent, or day. Sync models puts Magpie models into the Pi, Codex, and Claude Code pickers, and you can route one thread or a whole provider through Magpie. Gateway keys stay on the VesnALIA server.

mane-control.description: Switch Ponytail between Off, Lite, Full, and Ultra in one click, so how hard the agent works matches the task in front of you. A horse button beside the thread composer lists the four modes with a line on what each one does, and keeps the active mode in view. Picking a mode sends the /ponytail command for you, and those commands collapse into compact status pills in the transcript instead of stray slash-command lines. Needs the Ponytail skill installed for the thread's provider, and the control stays disabled until it finds one.

markdown-editor.description: Edit a markdown file in the tab you were already reading it in, and save it with Cmd+S. Preview renders the file the way VesnALIA renders a chat message, including the images it points at, and Raw gives you the source in an editable pane, with unsaved text carrying between the two. Selecting text in Preview offers an Add to chat button that quotes it into the composer under the file's path. A pencil on markdown files in the changes panel opens the one you are reading a diff of. Every save checks the file's hash first, so an edit an agent made while you were typing gives you a choice between reloading and overwriting instead of a silent clobber. Works on files in a project workspace, on a host, or in a thread's storage. Requires VesnALIA 0.43 or later, and needs no account or external service.

markdown-reader.description: Markdown source mixes document content with formatting syntax. Markdown Reader provides formatted Preview, exact Raw text, and heading navigation in the same read-only VesnALIA file tab. Open workspace, host, and thread-storage files, follow supported links, preview images, and refresh content without editing it. Remote images contact their source servers; no paid account or separate service is required. Requires VesnALIA 0.45+ and Plugin SDK >=0.6.15 <0.7; supports UTF-8 text up to 1 MiB, with VesnALIA preview available for unsupported files.

New releases follow mattpocock/skills daily; some skills use Git or GitHub CLI, and no account is needed.

mattermost.description: Bring work conversations into your VesnALIA threads. Search and link conversations, quote context, preview attachments, and keep personal starred and pinned conversations. Requires the mm CLI on an enrolled VesnALIA host and a signed-in Mattermost account.

maxwell.description: Keep Maxwell beside your VesnALIA conversations.

mcp-hub.description: Keeps MCP servers for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Kimi and OpenCode in one file and writes each harness its own config. Edit URL or command, headers and environment variables as key/value rows. Secrets live in a git-ignored mcp.local.json and are referenced as ${VAR}.
