mcp-manager.description: Find and manage MCP connections across five coding harnesses. Filter by harness, organize with tags, reconnect, or remove a configuration with a backup. Requires an enrolled VesnALIA host and installed harness CLIs for status checks and sign-in.

md-editor.description: Edit agent-written Markdown as a formatted document, and send any passage to the chat with its file path and line numbers. Callouts, collapsible details, footnotes, raw HTML and YAML properties render in place and save back unchanged, so opening a file never rewrites it. Mermaid flowcharts are edited by right-click (add a block or a yes/no branch, change a shape, delete), and LaTeX, code highlighting for 37 languages and directory trees render alongside. Files open from the machine and folder of the thread they came from, and autosave stops instead of overwriting a change an agent made underneath you. Adds a markdown-pro agent skill and a close-others and pin menu on the side-panel tabs; needs VesnALIA 0.43 or later and no account or external service.

md-prompt.description: Read Markdown and code with live formatting as you write your prompt. Code fences gain syntax colours before you close them. Toggle highlighting in the composer, settings or CLI without changing the text sent to your agent. Requires VesnALIA 0.47 or later; no external service, account or API key.

media-viewer.description: Zoom into screenshots, step through recordings and play audio in VesnALIA's right panel instead of a fit-only preview. Drag to pan, pinch or Ctrl-scroll to zoom at the pointer, and double-click to switch between Fit and a close-up. Previous and next step through every image, video and audio file in the same folder. Videos get frame stepping, seeking and speeds from 0.25× to 2×, and agents can show the same viewer inline in a reply with a ::media directive.

meetings.description: Keep recordings, transcripts and action items from Zoom, Google Meet, Telemost and Jitsi calls together. Record and transcribe Russian speech on a Linux x64 or arm64 host with Chrome, Xvfb, PulseAudio, ffmpeg and the separately installed GigaAM plugin or your own transcription server. Use five built-in or custom summary templates, transcript search, timecoded Q&A, optional calendar auto-join and external agents through MCP or REST. A VesnALIA agent or an optional model API writes summaries; calendar sync needs Google OAuth or an ICS feed, and admission can require a platform account.

memory-explorer.description: See what your agents remember: VesnALIA memory as a searchable table and a zoomable link graph, with a detail drawer for each memory. Search and filter every global and project memory, follow the links between memories, and see what links back to each one. Confirm or discard the preferences agents marked unconfirmed, and keep your own notes on people, teams and initiatives. Needs VesnALIA 0.48 or later and VesnALIA's Memory plugin.

message-date-time.description: Puts the date and time above every message in a thread, yours and the agent's. Labels read "Today, 2:34 PM", "Yesterday, 22:10" or "Oct 3, 9:15 AM", and older messages add the year. Choose English or Russian and a 12- or 24-hour clock, or let the plugin follow your computer's settings. A VesnALIA update can hide the labels until the plugin catches up; the chat keeps working.

message-timestamps.description: Shows the time you sent each message next to your bubbles in VesnALIA chat windows.

miku.description: Keep Hatsune Miku beside you while you work, with a roaming pixel-art companion that reacts to activity across VesnALIA. Drag her out of the way, keep her in place, or hide her from the command palette. Enable agent-powered comments using a configured VesnALIA provider and its account or usage allowance. Optional synthesized voice runs locally and requires FFmpeg with Flite and Rubber Band on the VesnALIA server.

millivolt.description: See every AI request your agents make, and what it cost, without leaving VesnALIA. The plugin installs millivolt for you or adopts a deployment you already run, then keeps it current on each VesnALIA start. Its sidebar shows live requests, tokens, cost and latency next to the full millivolt dashboard for settings, holds and debugging. Needs Docker; millivolt keeps its own SQLite history in a Docker volume and listens on loopback only.

minimap.description: A scrollbar you can read: a strip along the right edge of each thread, drawn like VS Code's minimap, with one rectangle per message, as tall as the message and coloured by kind (your messages, agent replies, work, errors, system notes). Drag its slider to scrub, click to glide there, scroll the wheel over it, or hover to see the rows around the pointer with an icon and the start of each one's text. It replaces VesnALIA's fading scrollbar, or keeps it beside the strip, casts a soft shade on a dark theme, and a settings panel in the thread menu sets the size, colours, slider, note and scrolling while you watch. It reads only what changed while a turn works and nothing while the strip is not shown. Requires VesnALIA 0.49 or later.

minus.description: Hide the VesnALIA controls you never click and fold runs of tool calls into one "Called N tools" row. Twenty-seven switches in Settings, grouped by area, each remove one element: back/forward buttons, sidebar and panel toggles, "..." menus, the Commit and "Open in" buttons, the prompt box buttons and the items under it, the message navigator, message and code block hover buttons, thinking rows, thread provider icons, and the macOS workbench padding. Changes apply in every open window without a reload, and keyboard shortcuts keep working for hidden controls. A VesnALIA update that renames an element can bring it back until the plugin catches up.

moa.description: Compare two independent perspectives before your chat model acts on each request. Enable MoA per chat, share model and fallback settings across chats, and inspect each participant’s input, answer and delivery receipt from the message history. Advisors retain separate sessions, and active models can continue beyond a long-wait notice. Uses your configured VesnALIA providers and accounts, adding model calls, latency and provider usage; remote file reads require the separately installed File Gateway plugin.

moa-provider.description: Get a second and third opinion on every message before one agent changes your files. Each preset you build becomes a model in the model picker: up to six advisor models answer in parallel, then an aggregator model reads their notes and does the work. A live panel in the thread shows what each advisor is doing and its answer as it streams. Type /moa in any other thread to put a question to the same advisors, or have the aggregator check in with them every few tool calls. Uses the providers you already installed and signed in to; each advisor adds a model turn to every message, and what an advisor reads goes to its model's provider.

model-effort-badges.description: See each thread’s model and reasoning effort in the VesnALIA sidebar. Hover for the full name.

model-favicons.description: Gives every agent its own logo, so custom ACP agents stop sharing one generic icon. Pick a mark per provider from the sidebar or the VesnALIA model-favicons command, and nine bundled marks cover GLM, Kimi, MiniMax Code, OpenCode, Qwen Code, Claude, Codex, and Gemini. Applies in the model picker and every provider list, in light and dark. Needs VesnALIA 0.49 or newer and a configured ACP provider.

model-presets.description: Adds a preset menu to the New thread composer that sets provider, model, effort, and speed in one step, applies custom instructions to threads started with it, and opens by keyboard shortcut with number keys to pick.

model-pricing.description: Compare what every AI model costs per million tokens, across Anthropic, OpenAI, Fireworks AI, Ollama Cloud and OpenRouter, in one table. A Relative column ranks each model against the cheapest one on screen, weighted by an input/output blend you choose. Each row also gives the context window, the longest reply, and whether the model can reason, call tools or return structured output. Sort by any column, search by name, hide a provider with its legend dot, and open any model's own page from its row. Prices come from the public models.dev catalog and OpenRouter's model list and are kept for twelve hours; no account or key is needed, but the machine running the VesnALIA server must reach both sites.

model-visibility.description: Keep the model picker short without losing access to any model. Move chosen model IDs out of the main list and into More models, where they stay selectable and searchable. Hide models per provider, with Hide all for a whole catalog and a Configure... shortcut in More models. Hiding is display-only: the selected model, reasoning level, service tier, and provider catalogs are unchanged. Experimental and desktop-only for VesnALIA 0.47.1; the compact picker fails open, and a future picker layout change may need a plugin update.

monokai.description: A dark Monokai-family theme for VesnALIA: one meaning per hue, a single text ladder, and a matching terminal palette.

multi-repo-git.description: Keep related projects and conversations within reach without replacing VesnALIA's native workspace tree. Group subprojects into workspaces and page each project's chat families (1–100, default 5). Recent loads chats 50 at a time as you scroll and searches titles and project names across all visible, non-archived chats with saved messages. Work and unread status remain visible together, including activity in child chats. Includes repository-local Source Control; requires VesnALIA 0.48.1+, SDK 0.6.104+, Node 24.20.0+ and the built-in thread-list, with no external service or paid account.

muse.description: Runs VesnALIA chats on the Muse personal assistant (muse.ai) through your own signed-in Muse accounts. Tools, MCP servers and skills run on your machine; replies stream into the VesnALIA chat. Several accounts with parallel chats, each account's weekly limit on the settings screen, and one Chrome sign-in copied to every connected machine. Not the Muse Code CLI plugin.

my-jira.description: See every Jira ticket assigned to you in one VesnALIA tab, filtered and grouped the way you work, and move it along without opening Jira. Filter by status and type, search by key or words, and group by status, initiative and epic, or the boards that list each ticket. Open a ticket beside the list to read its lineage, description, subtasks and comments, then step to the next one with Previous and Next or the keyboard. Change a status in place from the moves your workflow allows. Needs Jira Cloud with Atlassian's Rovo MCP server allowed for your organization; you sign in with Atlassian in the browser and set up nothing else.

my-tasks.description: Plan personal work with sections, nested steps and optional agent assistance. Review suggestions before accepting them. Assistance requires an authenticated Codex CLI and uses provider quota.

nanogpt-provider.description: Run alia threads on NanoGPT's models, unlocked by your own API key. nav-rail.description: Make more room for threads with a vertical strip of sidebar icons. Keep your saved navigation order and hidden destinations, with controls to rearrange them or open panels in a split. Start a new thread from the sidebar header, and use hover labels, selected states, and badges to find your way. nested-sidebar.description: Give every project a stable place in the sidebar, with its worktrees and agent threads underneath it. noema.description: Bridges VesnALIA threads to your own Noema server over its Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint for durable, searchable memory across sessions.

noisegate.description: Agent-invoked noise suppression — the agent can check short acknowledgements and filler against known noise patterns before sending.

noted.description: Point at the exact part of an agent's HTML or Markdown artifact and send that feedback straight to its thread. notify.description: Sends a native macOS notification when a VesnALIA thread finishes or fails, and adds a notify_user agent tool plus a VesnALIA notify command.

notify-feed.description: Keep your conversation from drowning in child-thread reports when a thread delegates work. Background messages and completion notices move to a Notifications tab beside the feed. Browse updates by thread or day, and reply directly from the panel. Works inside VesnALIA with no external service.

notion-theme.description: Give VesnALIA Notion's page colours and type in light and dark, then pick Default, Serif or Mono for messages. Menus, dialogs, switches and your own bubble follow those shapes; markdown in the thread uses Notion's inline code, quotes, headings and tables. Hover cards close when the pointer leaves, and a click pins them. A notice on the prompt box appears when a provider window is exhausted and can retry at reset. No account; licensed Notion fonts are named first, then system fallbacks.

now-playing.description: Play, pause, and skip tracks from a small player in the VesnALIA sidebar footer. The player shows the current track with album art, a seek bar, shuffle, repeat, and volume, in one of seven styles: Default, Minimal, Cover, Hi-Fi, Terminal, Pocket, and the alia-amp skin. The styles follow your VesnALIA theme in light and dark mode, and four of them take an accent color. By default the player follows the app that is playing, and a setting locks it to Spotify or Apple Music. The VesnALIA music command gives terminals and agents the same controls. On macOS, Spotify needs its desktop app, and macOS asks once for permission to control each app. Covers for streamed Apple Music tracks come from Apple's iTunes Search API, which receives the artist and title; a setting turns this off.

nudge.description: Continue or retry the agent from an empty composer. Play replaces Send while the draft is empty, starts idle threads without a user bubble, and retries failed turns by reference. Hidden while the agent is running. Also available as VesnALIA nudge. No account or API key.

nudger.description: Agents stop halfway and wait for you to type “go on”. Nudger types it for you: Jev reads each stopped thread and nudges only unfinished work, never past a blocker or a request for permission. Bring your own Jev API key.

ocean-dark.description: Give VesnALIA blue-grey surfaces, sky-blue accents and teal highlights. Matching syntax and terminal palettes keep code previews and diffs coordinated. Adapts T3 Code's Ocean dark palette and stays dark in Light, Dark or System mode. Requires VesnALIA 0.47.1 or later and a compatible Plugin SDK; no account or external service is needed.

oddship-gitea.description: Read Gitea issues and pull requests and prepare agent work without leaving VesnALIA. Choose an account and repository, filter the current page, and read descriptions and comments. Requires the tea CLI with an authenticated login on the selected VesnALIA host.

oddship-gitlab.description: Work through GitLab issues and merge requests inside VesnALIA. Read discussions, inspect pipeline status, update supported item fields, and start agent work or reviews. Requires glab installed and authenticated on the VesnALIA server.

office-viewer.description: Opens Excel, Word, PowerPoint, PDF, images and video right in VesnALIA's side panel, on any device you browse from. Spreadsheets recalculate live formulas and save edits to .xlsx and .csv without touching the formatting. Pictures open in an editor for arrows, boxes, text, numbered steps, blur and crop, and the result goes straight into the chat. Select cells, a PDF passage or a slide and quote it to the agent. Runs locally: no account, API key or external service.

ollama-fleet.description: Route local inference across your Ollama servers and see which model handled each job. Inspect health and model inventory, with bounded fallback and job history. Requires VesnALIA and a reachable Ollama server; Agent Board 0.6.0 or newer is an optional companion.

ollama-usage.description: Shows what is left in the Ollama Cloud monthly credit pool, with its reset date and the money already spent, in VesnALIA's usage panel. The panel reads only the OpenCode Go and Claude Code subscriptions, so an Ollama Cloud plan has no row there; this adds the pool as a dollar window beside them. Spend for the last day, week or month comes with a per-model breakdown, and VesnALIA ollama-usage prints the same numbers in a terminal. Needs an Ollama Cloud account with an API key on the host, either OLLAMA_API_KEY or the sign-in OpenCode already stored.

omarchy.description: Keeps VesnALIA desktop and PWA colors in step with the active Omarchy theme, including light/dark mode, ANSI and code colors, favicon tinting, and animated transitions, while leaving the native mobile app independent.

omp-agents.description: Name an OMP subagent in the composer instead of describing it. Type @, pick a row, and the pill carries the agent's specialization, tools, model, and definition file to the model at send time. The menu appears only on OMP threads; on another provider a send carrying an OMP mention is refused with the reason. Requires the omp CLI and a thread on the omp provider.

omp-subagents.description: Watch OMP subagents work instead of staring at a "Ran tool" row. Each spawn gets a live line per agent under it in the dialog, and the thread header opens a panel with every agent's status, model, tokens, cost, transcript and final output. A box in the panel messages the OMP session, and a VesnALIA omp-subagents command gives agents the same view. Requires threads on the omp provider and the omp CLI on the machine that runs them.

open-in-window.description: Opens any thread in its own browser tab or window from the thread's "..." menu, so two threads can stay open side by side. Adds Open in new window to the sidebar row's menu, its right-click menu, and the thread header's menu. Opens the same link Copy link copies, exactly as a target="_blank" link would, so your browser's own tab and window settings decide where it lands. Nothing to configure, no commands, and no network access.

opencode2.description: Run VesnALIA threads on any model you've connected to OpenCode v2, with VesnALIA's rewind, fork, steering, and permission modes intact. Tool calls show as native VesnALIA rows, including live command output and file changes built from OpenCode's own patches. VesnALIA dynamic tools, skills, and the VesnALIA CLI work inside OpenCode sessions. Needs OpenCode v2 (2.0.26 or newer, installed as opencode2) on the host and a model provider connected with opencode2 auth login.

openrouter-inference.description: Choose the OpenRouter model that writes your thread titles and commit messages. Search models by name or ID, compare token prices and context sizes, and test a sample title before switching. Change the selected model from settings whenever you want. Requires an OpenRouter API key; prompts, thread text, and diffs go to OpenRouter and the selected model provider, with charges billed to your account.

openspec.description: Browse OpenSpec changes and specifications, track task progress, and launch linked agents.

openspec-review.description: Comment on quoted text in OpenSpec proposals, designs and specs, and send the comments to the agent in the chat.

openui.description: Turns agent replies into dashboards, reports, plans and forms you can read at a glance and click, right in the chat. Agents write OpenUI Lang, and the plugin draws it with OpenUI's React component library plus about 70 components of its own: gauges, heatmaps, timelines, roadmaps, kanban boards, test and coverage reports, diffs and maps. Plans, decisions, choices, quizzes and forms send your answer back into the thread as your next message. Components for VesnALIA show the thread's changed files, commits, pull request and other threads live. Adds about 3,000 tokens of instructions to sessions whose replies you read, and Map and ImageSearch fetch from OpenStreetMap, Photon, Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons unless you turn web lookups off.

operator-inbox.description: Adds a project-scoped inbox where VesnALIA agents leave durable messages and operators reply through native threads.

orchestrator-mode.description: Keep one thread as the planner and send every unit of work to its own worker thread. A watchdog checks new timeline work at the guard and block levels, records direct work the parent did itself, and sends up to three corrective messages or stops the turn. Toggle a thread from the composer, its + menu or `alia orchestrator-mode`, and switch the mode on for every new thread you start. Workers share the parent's environment and provider, so they need no extra service; requires VesnALIA 0.44 or newer.

otel.description: Send per-turn token, cost and quota data from VesnALIA to the OpenTelemetry collector you already run. Each finished turn becomes a span with the model, input, output and cache tokens, and cost when the provider reports it; child threads join the trace of their root thread. Histograms and counters track token usage, turn duration, cost, turns and thread transitions, and gauges follow provider quota windows (used percent, reset time). Prompts, replies, tool text, thread titles, file paths and error messages are never exported, and no setting turns that on. Needs an OpenTelemetry collector that you run; nothing is sent until you set its OTLP/HTTP endpoint.

pad.description: Keep notes beside your work in a local Markdown outline, with keyboard editing and optional agent reviews. Capture notes from the panel, the `alia pad add` command, or the `pad_add` agent tool. Notes stay on your VesnALIA server with local Git history; optional reviews send pending notes to your chosen agent provider and use its normal quota or billing. Requires VesnALIA 0.49.0 or later and Git.

pane-workspaces.description: Switch whole pane arrangements for projects, thread groups and personal threads. Create thread workspaces, switch from sidebar controls or a searchable picker, and recover the previous layout. Layouts remain browser-local; stock VesnALIA reloads on a switch. Requires VesnALIA 0.42+ and uses internal host interfaces; disable the previous workspaces plugin before installing this renamed package.

password-gate.description: Locks the VesnALIA app behind a password, so an unattended window stops exposing your threads. Set the password in Settings, and every window shows an unlock panel until someone enters it. Tick Trust this device once and that browser skips the prompt until the trust window ends. Forgot it? The panel covers the Settings page, so run `alia password-gate reset` in a terminal to open the app again. The lock is the app window, not your data: it does not stop anyone who can run commands on the VesnALIA machine or reach its port.

peek.description: See what a plugin would change in VesnALIA before you install it. Every card in the plugin store gets a Preview button that lists the surfaces the plugin would add — a sidebar page, a thread-header button, a settings section — each with the plugin's own name for it. The same report names the settings it would create and flags wide access: a full-trust daemon, a script that can rewrite any part of the VesnALIA UI, or permission to run commands on your machine. Nothing is installed or executed to produce it, because Peek reads the exact release's files as text from the VesnALIA app, npm, or GitHub. No account or token is required, and the same report is available to you and your agents through VesnALIA peek show.

pets.description: Adds a pixel companion to the VesnALIA window that mirrors your fleet, walks to threads waiting on you, and earns XP from finished turns.

pi-command-sync.description: Run Pi's own slash commands inside a VesnALIA thread instead of paying a model turn for them. The composer menu lists every command the Pi session has loaded, including extension and prompt commands VesnALIA cannot see on its own. /session, /thinking, /model, /name and /reload answer from the addon with no model request, and terminal-only controls such as /login or /resume explain the limitation instead of falling through to the model. Needs a one-time patch to VesnALIA's installed Pi provider bundle, applied with the checked script in the repository, because VesnALIA 0.45.0 has no API for this. Linux hosts only; macOS is untested and Windows is refused.

pinch-zoom.description: Resize VesnALIA's chat, composer and terminal text with a pinch, or switch a setting to scale the whole app. Text scales from 75% to 200%; settings make the composer and terminal half to double the chat size, and terminals re-wrap to their new width when you let go. A pinch over a terminal fine-tunes it on that device. Works with a touchscreen, a trackpad pinch, or Ctrl and the mouse wheel, and a Settings section has A−, A+ and Reset buttons. Terminal sizing and chat-only scaling hook into VesnALIA's internal components, so a VesnALIA update can break them until the plugin catches up; whole-app text sizing does not depend on them.

pinned-turns.description: Keep the question you are reading under and the agent's last answer in view while you scroll a long thread. Click either one to jump back to it; the page's address and the back button stay as they were. A counter such as 7/23 shows which turn you are on, and a turn that is still running pulses. A Pinned turns submenu in the thread's actions menu switches the bar and each option on or off. It reads VesnALIA's timeline layout, which is not a documented interface, so a VesnALIA update may need a plugin update. Requires VesnALIA 0.48 or later.

plain-paste.description: Pastes only the text of the clipboard into the message box with ⇧⌘V, never its images or attachments. The text replaces any selection and keeps its line breaks. If the clipboard holds no text, nothing is pasted and a notice says why. Works in the message box only, in VesnALIA Desktop on macOS. Requires VesnALIA 0.46+ and Plugin SDK 0.6.49+.

plan-mode.description: Lock agents into a read-only planning phase before they touch code or run commands. Refuses execution requests and directs you to switch to Implement mode when ready to proceed. Features instant toggling via Shift+Tab or the composer button, a distinctive dashed border while active, and configurable default-on settings for new chats. Injects instructions silently at turn submit without displaying in the prompt or timeline.

plan-progress.description: Follow the agent's plan above the message box, with stages, steps and status for questions, errors and completion. Fold the progress block or hide and restore individual plans. See observed helper activity and estimated answer speed. Bounded reminders can prompt agents to create or update plans. Plan data stays on your VesnALIA server; no extra account or API key.

play-continue.description: Stop a run with a double Escape and pick up a stopped turn with one Play click. Two Escape presses within 400 ms press VesnALIA's own Stop button, and the Stop icon shows Esc after the first press. plugin-updates.description: Shows which installed plugins have updates and installs them for you, including newer releases outside a plugin's version range. A count on the nav icon and a one-time toast flag each new version. Compatible updates install in place, singly or all at once; out-of-range ones reinstall at the new release with settings restored and rollback on failure. Requires git and network access to each plugin's repository.

plugin-vault.description: Label and annotate VesnALIA plugins right on the Plugins page. Custom labels, an automatic Installed label, and blurred names for plugins you rejected.

plugin-workshop.description: Turns a few sentences into an installed VesnALIA plugin, with one agent per stage from spec and mockup to code, review and rollout.

pokecut-theme.description: Turns VesnALIA into a soft dashboard: a gray shell, the thread as a raised panel, white cards and a pink-violet accent, light and dark. The composer gets even chips for project, machine and access, a gradient send button and a context line that fills as the window does. Expanded work groups read as one card with right-aligned durations and red error chips, and messages show their time on hover. A footer switch flips light, dark or system, and each chat feature can be turned off in English or Russian settings.

pokemon.description: Build your Pokémon collection as you finish work in VesnALIA. Archive a thread to catch one of 1,025 species, then track your progress and duplicate catches in the Pokédex. Explore each catch’s artwork, types, stats, abilities, and cry. Uses free PokeAPI data and GitHub-hosted media.

pokemon-catcher.description: Turn shipped engineering work into Pokémon catches, evolutions, and a collection that grows across VesnALIA threads. Earn rewards from local branches and worktrees, or selected GitHub repositories and Shortcut, Jira, or GitHub Issues. Choose any catch as an evolving companion, incubate Eggs through token usage, and filter the collection by type, rarity, generation, or shiny status. GitHub, Shortcut, and Jira connections require user-supplied credentials; the plugin also requests data, sprites, and cries from PokéAPI-hosted services. Requires VesnALIA 0.43+ and Plugin SDK 0.4.87+.

polza.description: Run alia threads on polza.ai models and pay in rubles from one Polza balance. Sign in with your Polza account; the plugin stores the issued key on the VesnALIA server. Choose which catalog models the picker offers, in your order, with prices and context size shown. The sidebar shows the available balance and the key's remaining spend limit, and each thread shows an estimated spend and cache hit rate above the composer. Polza also works as VesnALIA's AI service for thread titles and commit messages on a small model you choose. Threads run the Claude Code CLI against Polza, so Claude Code's tools, permission modes, plan mode and skills keep working; the plugin installs the CLI when it is missing. Needs a Polza account with balance.

pool-usage.description: See how much of each provider's capacity is in use and when it frees up, right in the sidebar footer. Each provider gets its logo and one percentage, with accounts weighed by their plans, so a Claude Max 20x seat counts twenty times a Pro seat. Clicking a number opens a card with the account count and when the total drops next. When Account Pooler's Claude or Codex accounts hold resets, the card offers the one that frees the most capacity and spends it only after you confirm. Covers Account Pooler's accounts and any provider that reports usage to VesnALIA, such as Cursor; Account Pooler is optional.

pr-manager.description: Shows your open GitHub pull requests and recent merges, one project at a time, with their CI and review state summarised as failing, feedback, draft, open, approved, part approved, waiting or merged, and opens or links the VesnALIA worktree thread for the one you pick.

pr-notes.description: Review pull requests, keep private notes, and chat with agents in VesnALIA. Find assigned PRs and review requests, inspect diffs and check results, and post comments or manage PRs using your GitHub access. PR details and saved notes become context in VesnALIA's native chat. Requires GitHub CLI signed in on the VesnALIA server; chat needs a configured agent provider and may incur its charges.

pr-xray.description: Understand a pull request before you judge it. PR X-ray groups the diff by concern and puts it in reading order, then explains it with a walkthrough, diagrams and the spots worth a closer look. Ask questions as you read, and comment or submit your review on GitHub without leaving VesnALIA.

preset-buttons.description: Starts a new thread on the harness you meant to use, not the one the last thread left behind. Four buttons in the New thread composer apply a saved provider, model, and reasoning level in one click. A settings editor builds the buttons from VesnALIA's live provider catalogue, so no JSON and no reload. The strip holds one row beside the project picker and never wraps.

preset-sync.description: Synchronizes portable VesnALIA plugins and settings across computers through a Git repository.

prime-agent-acp.description: Runs VesnALIA threads on Prime Agent (by Prime Intellect) through its native ACP protocol, with model discovery and reasoning level support. Installing the provider requires an explicit `alia prime-agent install` command that downloads and installs the official prime-agent binary from Prime Intellect; thread content is processed by Prime Intellect.

productive.description: Work a Productive.io board without leaving VesnALIA, and hand a ticket to an agent in one click. Kanban lanes group by workflow status or by task list, so the columns match the board you already use, and dragging a card writes the change back to Productive. Start a thread from any ticket, optionally in its own git worktree, with the ticket's fields as context. Agents reach the same board through a `alia productive` command. Needs a Productive.io account and an API token.

progressive-skill.description: Smart skill index compaction — usage-ranked, budget-capped skill lists so agents load the right skills.

project-colors.description: Organize busy sidebars by giving every project its own color. Choose from seven colors; project headings, nested threads, and conversation titles carry the project's visual identity. Choices stay local to each VesnALIA client, and the plugin uses no external service or account.

project-explorer.description: Browse and edit the files behind a thread in the side panel, with git status colouring every name the way VS Code does. Modified files read amber, new files green, deleted red, and a collapsed folder inherits the colour of whatever changed inside it. Saving sends back the hash the file had when you opened it, so a change an agent made underneath you reports a conflict instead of being overwritten. Dotfiles such as .claude and .env appear, and directories load one level at a time, so a repository with node_modules opens as quickly as an empty one. Needs a thread whose environment has a workspace; git colours need that workspace to be a git repository.

project-folders.description: Organize VesnALIA chats into projects and nested sections that are real folders, so each chat starts in its own working directory. Each project and section can carry AGENTS.md rules from shared or own templates, plus custom rules for files or VesnALIA sessions and a startup instruction for new chats. Style the sidebar tree with 118 icons or any emoji, 12 colors, fills and four presets, per level, per project or per section. Archive finished sections with their files and chats and restore them later, keep working copies on several devices, and move projects or sections without breaking existing chats. Requires VesnALIA 0.43+ and macOS or Linux devices; the interface comes in 11 languages with English by default.

project-instructions.description: Gives each VesnALIA project its own standing instructions and adds them to the system prompt of every thread in that project, without writing anything into the repository.

project-page.description: Open a project's homepage from its name in VesnALIA's sidebar. The homepage renders the checkout's README, links to the configured repository, and starts a new thread in that project. Reads go through VesnALIA's project APIs and the project's enrolled host, so a remote browser client sees the same README as a local window. The sidebar chevron still expands and collapses threads, and disabling the plugin restores the original sidebar. Requires VesnALIA 0.43.1 or later with Plugin SDK 0.4.87 or later.

project-themes.description: Give every project its own color, so threads and workspaces are easier to recognize at a glance. Tint thread rows, browser tabs, and the workspace background independently. Choose from eight presets or a custom color; settings sync across VesnALIA windows. Requires VesnALIA 0.45 or later and no external service.

project-usage-sort.description: Puts the projects you work in most at the top of VesnALIA's project lists, re-ranked every hour from your own thread activity. Each thread counts toward its project, and its weight halves every 14 days, so this week's work outranks last quarter's. The order lands in VesnALIA's own project order, which the new-thread project picker uses, and in the built-in sidebar's project sections. Run alia project-usage-sort preview to see the ranking before anything moves; it runs on your VesnALIA server and calls no external service.

prolepsia.description: Create probabilistic forecasts and check their progress from VesnALIA with your Prolepsia account. Discover and call forecasting and question tools through your agent or the VesnALIA prolepsia command. Requires a Prolepsia API key; forecast runs consume Prolepsia credits.

prompt-enhancer.description: Rewrites the composer draft into a clearer prompt through a hidden VesnALIA thread, keeping follow-ups short, preserving @mentions and file paths, and offering Undo.

prompt-log.description: Lists every prompt you sent in a thread in a Prompts side-panel tab, newest first and grouped by day, with a filter, a marker on the prompt being worked on, and a button that puts any earlier prompt back in the composer.

prompt-shaper.description: Turns a rough draft into a clear, complete prompt that you review before sending. Choose Improve prompt and a hidden helper agent rewrites only the draft, then returns it in place of your text. Attachments stay attached, and you can undo the rewrite. Each rewrite runs one short turn on a provider you already use.

prompts.description: Stashes prompts you write while an agent is busy and injects, schedules, or auto-sends them when it next goes idle, alongside a searchable snippet library with {{fill-in}} templates.

provider-authentication.description: Authenticates and reauthenticates Claude Code on connected VesnALIA machines from VesnALIA settings.

provider-brand-marks.description: Draws each provider logo in its own brand colour — Anthropic clay, OpenAI green, Pi steel blue, Hermes ultramarine — instead of the one monochrome mask they all share. Fits every colour to the palette you already use, in light and dark mode, without replacing your theme.

provider-muse.description: Adds Meta's Muse Code as a VesnALIA provider over its own session protocol: streamed timeline, approvals, subagents, model picker, health, and the plan's own 5-hour and weekly usage limits as Muse reports them.

provider-retry-advanced.description: Keeps VesnALIA's bundled overload and subscription-limit retries and resumes turns after lost connectivity. Optional, off by default: Claude Code UltraCode workflow recovery, a stalled-turn watchdog and continuation follow-ups. A fresh install observes until armed. Disable the bundled Provider retry before use.

provider-usage.description: Shows how much of each provider's plan is left — every rate-limit window, percent remaining, and when it resets, including Muse Code's 5-hour and weekly limits — plus a 7/30/90-day token chart covering every provider, from local transcripts and VesnALIA's own usage events.

pstack.description: Puts 47 pstack engineering skills in every VesnALIA thread, with one setup step to choose the models they delegate to. Run /setup-pstack once and it reads this host's model list, then asks which model each pstack role should use. After that, /poteto-mode loads one of 23 playbooks and runs the other skills its steps need: reviews that put a second model on the change, tests, blast-radius checks, and prose cleanup. Every skill has its own switch, and none reach the model prompt until you invoke them. Needs VesnALIA 0.43 or newer, the VesnALIA CLI for skills that fan out to workers, and MCP servers or a webhook endpoint for the few skills that ask for them.

pstack-for-vesnalia.description: Use Lauren Tan's pstack skills in VesnALIA, synced daily from cursor/plugins with Cursor locations adapted for VesnALIA.

pulse.description: See what needs you from Slack, Gmail and Calendar on one live board, kept current by scheduled agent runs. Hourly, Daily and Weekly runs write items sorted into Now, Next, Later and Nice to Know, and Done or Snooze sticks across runs. Each item can carry prepared replies that copy to your clipboard and open the source; nothing is sent for you. A robot button hands an item to an agent thread that drafts the work for your review. Your agents need their own Slack, Gmail and Calendar access (MCP servers, CLIs or plugins), and every run uses your model quota.

px0.description: Review and edit a thread's codebase without leaving its VesnALIA conversation. Browse files, search the workspace, inspect symbols and references, and review Git diffs in a full-tab px0 workspace. px0's native editor saves changes and creates files or folders while refreshing Git, search, and language-server state. Requires px0 0.1.20 or newer on each workspace machine; remote panels require VesnALIA Connect.

px0-review.description: Review changes in your active worktree and send selected-code feedback to its VesnALIA thread. Browse files and diffs, edit code, and keep the existing conversation and provider. Downloads a pinned px0 fork on first use; remote access uses VesnALIA Connect.

qlik-sense.description: Agents read Qlik Sense Enterprise sheets and charts with filters. Sign in once, tick the reports agents may use, and choose which models may see the data.

quick-chat.description: Ask a question in a floating chat window without adding a thread to your sidebar. Open it with Mod+Shift+K, the command palette, or the sidebar chat icon, and drag it to a convenient corner. Return to recent chats or choose Open as thread when a conversation becomes project work. Uses your configured VesnALIA agent provider and its account; provider usage charges or subscription limits still apply.

quick-compose.description: Start a thread from a floating composer without leaving the page you’re on. Open it with Mod+Shift+L, or hand off the current thread with Mod+Shift+H; both shortcuts can be rebound in Settings → Keyboard. Keep your draft and selections when you dismiss it, then start the thread in the background when you’re ready. Requires VesnALIA 0.42+ and uses your configured agent provider and account.

quick-reply.description: Give your agent quick feedback by clicking on which lines you agree and disagree with. Ask for more detail on any line, or add a comment when a click isn't enough.
quick-reply.licenseNote: в package.json указано "GPL-3.0-only", в репозитории GPL-3.0

quick-thread.description: Opens a floating new-thread composer from anywhere with Ctrl/Cmd+N, so you can start a thread without leaving the one you are on. Enter creates and opens it; Ctrl/Cmd+Enter creates it in the background and shows a toast with an Open action. A command-palette row covers keyboards where the OS reserves the shortcut.

qwen-cli.description: Code with your Qwen account inside VesnALIA. Choose CLI-discovered models, switch between Plan and Build, and review tool requests in your thread. Requires a separately installed Qwen Code CLI and an eligible account; service quota or charges apply.

rad-binder.description: Turn VesnALIA into an 80s/90s school-binder cover, with neon confetti, striped edges and chunky toy-commercial shadows. The sidebar becomes a deep-purple binder spine where the open thread is a hot-pink sticker. The composer, your messages and inline cards get thick outlines and hard offset shadows, and headings switch to bold italic capitals. Works in light and dark, makes no network requests, and uses Futura and Avenir Next from macOS, falling back to your system sans elsewhere.

radar.description: See every pull request and issue that needs you, live in the sidebar, on GitHub and Delta, plus optional read-only Gitstream history. Saved lanes are queried live through your gh and dt CLIs, and config and caches stay in VesnALIA on your machine. Describe a queue in plain words and VesnALIA's configured AI drafts the lane; Focus hides repos everywhere and single items can be hidden too. From any row, start a review or triage thread with Radar's skills attached or rebase your own PR. Optional Context from Slack summarises the public Slack threads that link an item.

radar-sidebar.description: See which threads need you without opening each conversation. Group threads by activity, project or section, fold nested families, and preview goals and context usage on hover. Filter or save views, use keyboard and bulk actions, and keep navigation aligned with VesnALIA's sidebar settings. Requires VesnALIA 0.44+ and uses exclusive experimental sidebar slots; no external service or account.

read-aloud.description: Listen to any assistant message while you keep working, with speech that starts playing before the whole message is synthesized. A speaker button on every message row starts playback, and the player adds pause, stop, ten-second skips in both directions, and speeds from 0.75x to 2x that persist between sessions. Playback stops on its own when you switch threads or send a new prompt, and stopping cancels the synthesis stream instead of leaving it to finish unheard. Code blocks, link targets, and bare URLs are flattened out of the text first, so a voice reads prose instead of syntax. Speech uses Microsoft Edge's public neural voices over the network, so it needs an internet connection, but no account, API key, or paid service.

realtime-gateway.description: Runs Voice Mode's realtime sessions through a Vercel AI Gateway key, so voice bills to one gateway account and the VesnALIA host never needs an OpenAI key. Voice Mode asks installed connection plugins for a session; this one mints a single-use client secret from the gateway and returns its realtime URL with the secret already attached to the WebSocket handshake. Pick the model (gpt-realtime-mini by default), set an optional team scope, and run alia realtime-gateway test to confirm the handshake before relying on it. Needs a Vercel AI Gateway key with usage billing; no OpenAI key on this host.

recap.description: Generates concise, display-only summaries for VesnALIA threads on demand or after they become idle.

receipts.description: Compare coding-agent token usage and estimated API cost in one dashboard. Switch between 7, 30 and 90 days, with daily charts and breakdowns by model, project and day. Reads Claude Code, Codex, Hermes Agent, OpenCode and Pi usage from the VesnALIA server machine. Optional Cursor support requires a signed-in Cursor desktop app and its dashboard service; estimates are not subscription invoices.

reclaim.description: Find what filled your disk and get the space back, without guessing. Indexes the whole volume with no scan cap and counts hardlinks and APFS clones once, so shared copies do not inflate folder totals. Browse any folder by real subtree size, or work from a costed list of build output, idle dependencies, package caches, Xcode derived data and Docker layers, including compacting the Docker VM disk image that pruning alone never shrinks. Deletion is confined to roots you authorize, and a guard can clean up or hand the problem to an agent when space runs low. macOS and Linux, no account or external service.

references.description: Organize visual moodboards, design references, and inspirational websites directly beside your thread in VesnALIA IDE. Opens automatically in the thread panel when agents collect UI references. Extracts website metadata with OpenGraph previews and serves local project images with path-traversal protection. Lets you pin key stylistic anchors to your desk and inspect images in a full-screen lightbox.

rephrase.description: Adds a Re-phrase button to the prompt input that rewrites your draft with an agent and puts the result back in the composer.

responsibilities.description: Find failures, questions and unread results in VesnALIA. Filter threads, start child threads and optionally highlight managers.

retitle.description: Gives each thread a title that matches the conversation, not only its first message. After the first reply, a small model writes a new title: Haiku 4.5 on Claude Code, gpt-5.4-mini on Codex. Press ⌘⌥R, click the header button, or use the quick palette to rename any thread again, and turn on an emoji at the start of each title. Each rename runs one short session on the thread's own provider, so it needs no API key.

reveal-in-finder.description: Open the files an agent builds or exports with one click, instead of copying a path out of its reply. Each file or folder the agent hands over shows as a card with an icon, its name, format and size. A click on a file opens VesnALIA's preview, and Open in reveals it in Finder or opens it in its default app. A bundled skill tells agents when to hand over files this way. Finder and the default app open on the Mac running the VesnALIA server; no account or external service.
reveal-in-finder.licenseNote: в package.json указано "MIT", в репозитории permission

rewind.description: Undo an agent's file changes turn by turn, and let the conversation go back with them. Checkpoints the workspace before each message and after each turn, on every provider, with no setup. Preview a restore as a per-file diff before it runs, and undo it afterwards. Restore the files and edit your message in one step, or fork from any message into a worktree whose files are as they were then. Flags turns that ran git push, a deploy, or other effects a restore cannot undo. Needs git on the thread's machine; the workspace itself does not have to be a git repository.

role-picker.description: Choose a specialist in the composer without leaving the conversation. Includes six built-in roles and optionally connects to Agent Roles for custom profiles. Agent work uses your configured provider account and quota.

route.description: Hand mechanical edits to a cheaper agent, ask another model, or get a ranked decision without leaving the turn. route_worker runs a task on any VesnALIA harness and model you list, in the same environment, and returns its final message. route_ask sends one prompt to any OpenAI-compatible API, and route_decide asks a System One decision model such as TypeSafe Jev for a pick with probabilities. Each tool needs its own provider or endpoint and key, billed by that service.

rpiv-todo-renderer.description: Renders Pi rpiv-todo tasks in VesnALIA's native composer to-do panel.

rtk.description: Agent-invoked shell tool — rewrites commands through the external rtk CLI for filtered output on verbose builds, tests, and git diffs. Requires the rtk CLI; unrestricted shell access.

save-my-model.description: Give every VesnALIA machine its own provider, model, and reasoning preference. Configure each machine through VesnALIA's native picker and review or clear browser-local records without changing the built-in New Thread defaults.

scoped-skills.description: Give each skill only to the agents, models and projects that should have it, so image skills reach Codex and stay out of Claude Code. Each skill carries a list of agents plus optional model and project globs such as gpt-5* or *my-org/*, and a thread receives only the skills that match its agent, model and project. A preview shows what a thread on any agent, model and project would get. Import skill folders from the VesnALIA machine, or ask a thread to list or change a scope; a VesnALIA scoped-skills CLI does the same. Needs no account, API key or network access.

screen-sharing.description: See and control the screens of your Macs from inside VesnALIA, at your desk or from anywhere through remote access. A sidebar page shows each Mac connected to your VesnALIA with whether its Screen Sharing is on, and opens its screen in the page for your keyboard and mouse. Sessions to several Macs can be open at once, with View only, Send keys for shortcuts such as Command-Tab, Full screen, and a Clipboard menu that sends text either way or keeps both clipboards in sync, for the macOS account VesnALIA runs as on that Mac. Every new session asks for that Mac's own macOS user name and password, which VesnALIA never keeps, and a Close all pill ends every session at once. Requires VesnALIA 0.47 or later and macOS, with Screen Sharing turned on by you in System Settings on each Mac; it relies on experimental VesnALIA plugin APIs that may change between VesnALIA releases.

screenshot.description: Attach a selected area of your Mac's screen directly to a VesnALIA message. Use the native macOS crosshair from the camera button beside Send. Capture runs on the Mac displaying VesnALIA and preserves your draft text and attachments. Requires macOS, a connected VesnALIA host, screen recording permission, and browser local network access; no external service or paid account.

section-load-more.description: Keep long sidebar sections short, so opening one never pushes the others out of view. Each custom section and the Threads group shows its first 10 threads, with Load more and Show less at the end of the same section. Nothing is archived or moved, and the thread you have open always stays visible. Set the starting count and the batch size in the plugin settings.

security-guidance.description: Pattern-matched security warnings for code the agent writes — 25 rules covering unsafe deserialization, injection, XSS, and crypto footguns.

sentry-issues.description: Browses bounded, read-only Sentry issue snapshots across configured projects and opens searchable issue detail with optional local VesnALIA triage links.

server-status.description: Tracks host RAM usage as a ring around a sidebar footer button — amber from 80%, red above 90% — and opens a panel with CPU, memory, swap, disk, load average, uptime, and OS and kernel version.

session-history.description: See every Claude Code, Codex and Qwen Code session you ran outside VesnALIA, under the titles the agents gave them. The new-thread screen lists the sessions from the selected project's folders, and a Sessions page lists all of them with agent filters and search. Open any session to read its transcript, show its tool calls, or copy the command that resumes it in a terminal. Session files are read on the machine that runs VesnALIA and are never uploaded or changed.

session-log.description: Check what an agent actually ran, changed and decided, in one live log beside the chat. Messages, thinking, commands with their output and exit codes, tool calls, file diffs and subagent steps appear in timeline order, with a timestamp on every row and a duration on every command. The log follows new output as it arrives, opens failed commands by default, and filters to messages, thinking, tools or errors. Search covers the whole session, and single keys jump between rows, replies and errors. Open it with Mod+Shift+L or from the thread header; it reads VesnALIA's timeline and keeps no copy of the thread.

session-notes.description: Attaches private, thread-scoped notes to individual VesnALIA timeline messages, and never sends them to the agent's context.

sessions-switcher.description: Switch between seven recent sessions with Alt+Tab-style controls. Hold the shortcut modifier, select with the keyboard or pointer, then release to open. Choose horizontal cards or a vertical list, with provider icons and live running and unread indicators. No extra account or service is required.

shell-tasks.description: Keep agents moving while tests, builds, servers and watchers run in the background. Track each command in its thread, read live output, stop its process group and clear it when finished. Tasks survive plugin reloads, and successful or failed jobs can wake the agent with one batched completion message. Requires VesnALIA 0.43+, Plugin SDK 0.5.9+ and a Unix execution machine; commands run through `/bin/sh` with no external account.

shipyard.description: Drive coding tasks from idea to merge on a Kanban board, and nothing reaches your branch until you review it. Save ideas, brainstorm them with an agent, then queue them. Each task runs in its own VesnALIA thread and git worktree: a short triage picks the model and effort, an optional plan waits for your approval, and the agent builds, runs the checks, and reviews its own diff. Add skills to each stage, such as a planning skill for Plan. When an agent is stuck, it asks you, and your answer continues the same stage. Review in a side panel, request changes in the same session, open a pull request, or merge. Agents use the VesnALIA providers you already have; pull requests need a GitHub remote and the gh CLI.
