shop-kanban.description: Shows your VesnALIA threads as cards placed by live state, so you see at a glance which ones need you. Cards move on their own: a pending question or a failed run turns red at the top of Working, a reply that reports completion lands in Done, and threads you set aside wait in Parked. A working limit caps how many threads run at once: past it, a new thread waits in Queue and starts when a working one finishes, to pace spend. Each card carries a model-written title and summary, context-window fill, the harness icon, and the cost of the thread together with every child thread and subagent it started. Queue's In tab lists the Delta and GitHub pull requests waiting on you or your teams, each with a risk chip, approve and request-changes buttons, and a drafted thread that explains the change, and the Out tab tracks your own open and merged pull requests. The title bar searches every thread by what was said in it, archived ones included, and shows CPU, memory, disk and battery with the heaviest apps; on a Shopify account it also shows today's Shopify AI proxy spend. Titles, summaries and risk chips come from a pi-compatible CLI on the thread's host (default Claude Haiku 4.5), billed to that CLI's account; search needs qmd and the pull request lists need the dt or gh CLI, signed in, on a persistent host. Each is optional.

shortcut.description: Turn your assigned Shortcut stories into agent work in VesnALIA. Browse and reorder stories on a Kanban board, filter by workflow, and read story details. Start work from a story to move it to In Development and open an agent thread. Requires a Shortcut account and API token.

show-latest-threads.description: Shows only the threads you touched in the last 24, 48 or 72 hours, so the sidebar holds today's work. A switch and a 24h / 48h / 72h picker sit at the top of the list; turn the switch off to see every project. Pinned threads, sections and child threads keep their places, and a thread that is open, running or waiting for your answer stays visible whatever its age. Each row shows its status on the right as VesnALIA's own list does: a dot for unread, a spinner while the agent works, a question mark when it waits for you. English or Russian.

shuttle.description: Puts every pull request that needs you, from any server, in one Inbox grouped by what to do next. Each of your PRs keeps an agent thread that gets its new reviews, comments and failed checks, and fixes them or just passes them on. AI reviews come back as drafts you edit and post as yourself, and auto post, in shadow mode for the repositories you pick, records which findings it would have posted. Saved boards keep the PRs of a release or a handoff together with live status, across repositories and servers. Merge, comment, reply and resolve from Shuttle, with merges and reviews queued in the background on each server. GitHub works through your signed-in gh CLI; GitLab and other servers need a command adapter, a few shell commands you write that print JSON.

side-board.description: See every question, bug and todo your agent raises in one panel beside the thread, so nothing gets lost in the scroll. Items are numbered Q1, B1, T1: answer in chat with "Q3 clerk", or "go" to accept every recommendation. Agents add and close items themselves through the board_add and board_close tools, in every thread and with every provider. If a reply asks a question or finishes work without updating the board, the agent gets one reminder; you can turn this off in settings.

side-chat-links.description: Reopen a side chat from the message you started it on, instead of hunting for it. A thread icon appears under every message that has side chats, with a count when there are several. Click it to open a panel tab for that message, with one inner tab for each of its side chats. Rename a side chat by double-clicking its tab. Works with VesnALIA's bundled Side chat plugin, including side chats made before you install it, and needs VesnALIA 0.49 or later.

sidebar-plus.description: Keep active projects within reach and check thread status without leaving the sidebar. Pin, hide, reorder, and search projects in collapsible sections. Inspect branch and pull request details from thread menus, where you can also open a split, mark threads read or unread, pin, rename, archive, or delete them. Preferences stay in sync across VesnALIA windows.

sidebar-subtitles.description: Group sidebar destinations under your own headings. Drag sections or move them with arrow controls, hide sections and restore them from More. Edit headings with explicit Save, Cancel and Delete controls; your VesnALIA navigation order and visibility are preserved.

simple-sidebar-folders.description: Fold whole groups of sidebar projects, so work projects stay out of sight at home and personal ones stay out of sight at work. Drag a project by its name onto a folder to file it; VesnALIA's own project and thread rows stay as they are. A folded folder shows how many projects it holds, and a dot when a thread in it needs you. Folders are shared across your VesnALIA clients, and each client remembers which ones it keeps folded.

simple-summaries.description: Keep the latest thread summary in view as small italic text above the composer. Read the full summary with natural wrapping and no widget controls or badges. Generate summaries on demand or automatically after a thread becomes idle. Requires a configured VesnALIA provider and model; generation uses its normal subscription allowance or API billing.

skiff.description: Gives every thread its own throwaway Linux VM on your Mac, so nothing the agent installs or runs touches macOS. Claude Code and GitHub tokens stay in the macOS Keychain; the VM only holds placeholders that the skiff broker swaps for the real tokens on the way out. A fresh Ubuntu VM boots in about 4 seconds, is ready for the agent in under a minute, and is deleted when you archive the thread. Requires Apple Silicon, macOS 26, the open-source skiff CLI, a VesnALIA server access the VM can reach, such as VesnALIA Connect, and VesnALIA's own GitHub forwarding turned off.
skiff.licenseNote: в package.json указано "Apache-2.0", в репозитории permission

skill-library.description: Edit any skill VesnALIA discovers straight from the sidebar, so a downloaded skill becomes yours before it runs. Every skill on the machine — provider, plugin, built-in, and user — sits in one filterable list. Save carries a revision check, so a file changed on disk is refused instead of overwritten. Create new skills under ~/.vesnalia/skills, search skills.sh, and install registry entries without opening a terminal. Registry search and install need network access to skills.sh; everything else works offline.

skill-manager.description: Keep agent skills in sync from one hub. Find skills on skills.sh, install into selected agents, compare local copies, and check for updates. Requires Git and internet access for downloads and update checks.

skills.description: See every skill a thread's agent can use, where each one comes from and what it says, and add one to the chat from the panel or composer. A Skills tab in the thread's side panel groups them by origin — the project, the repository, your personal folder, an admin folder, a Claude Code or Codex plugin, or VesnALIA itself — and shows each one's SKILL.md, rendered, with its path on disk. Claude Code, Codex and Hermes threads have their skill folders read the way that agent reads them, in worktrees and on other enrolled machines too, so a name defined twice is listed once, under the copy the agent uses. Add to chat puts the skill in the message box as the same pill VesnALIA's / menu inserts and sends nothing, and a Skills button with a live count, or a keyboard command, opens the same list in VesnALIA's pop-up above the message box. Threads on other providers list VesnALIA's own skills and what VesnALIA's / menu offers. Needs VesnALIA 0.45 or later, and no account, key or network access.

slopcop.description: Automated PR review rules that dispatch VesnALIA agents.

smart-queue.description: Routes each message you send to a busy thread: corrections steer the running turn, and new tasks wait until it ends. TypeSafe's Jev model decides, reached with a TypeSafe, Vercel AI Gateway, OpenRouter, or OpenCode Zen key, or through any endpoint that speaks its System One API. Without a key, a model from a VesnALIA provider you already use decides in a hidden thread, and if nothing answers the message waits. Each decision sends the thread title, your recent requests, and the new message to that provider, which bills the usage.

sops.description: A SOPS editor for VesnALIA: see a repo's encrypted files, edit them in a table or as text, and save them encrypted again. Needs sops installed.
sops.licenseNote: в package.json указано "GPL-3.0-only", в репозитории GPL-3.0

souls.description: Give any thread a persona you define once: its job, voice, expertise and hard limits, the same in every thread that runs it. An agent interviews you in four to seven questions and puts the draft on a review card, and nothing is saved, edited or deleted until you approve. Pick a soul from the composer's + menu for an open thread or the next one, and a banner shows it with a pixel-art portrait that animates with what the agent is doing. After a context compaction the persona goes back in, and a parent thread can start a child already in character. Compare a soul with no soul on the same prompt before you rely on it. Souls stay in the plugin's own SQLite store with no account or external service, and a comparison spends model runs only when you start it.

spaces.description: Show only the projects you are working on by switching the sidebar between spaces such as Work and Personal. Each space has a name, an icon, its own projects and an optional sidebar tint; pick one from the menu in the sidebar header or press Ctrl+Alt+1 to 9 (⌃⌥ on macOS), and it reopens the thread you last had open there. All projects shows everything again. Edit Spaces sets each space's projects, icon, tint and order, turns folders dragged in from Explorer or Finder into projects, and keeps a project in no space visible in every space. `alia space` switches from a terminal or an agent. Needs VesnALIA 0.49 or later with the bundled Thread list plugin, and an active space groups the thread list by project.

specs.description: Give every project one shared set of spec documents that agents read before they change code. Specs link to any number of projects and live in one store, so they survive branches, worktrees, and new checkouts. Each project thread receives a compact index of its specs — pinned documents always, changed documents when they changed — and pulls full text only when an agent asks. Select a quote to leave a comment; open comments come back from the read tool as review feedback instead of silent edits. Every spec gets its own chat thread where the agent reads before answering and applies agreed changes with a revision check. Agents also get the VesnALIA specs command line and tools for search, annotate, attach, detach, and delete. Runs entirely inside VesnALIA: no account and no external service.

sql.description: Browse every Postgres database, complete SQL with schema awareness, and run queries from a panel or agent tools. New connections default to Agent write and Allow DDL on; duplicate connections from the menu.

steel-browser.description: Operate self-hosted Steel browser sessions from VesnALIA with project-scoped sessions, selectable Playwright or Jev execution, and inline viewing.

stelow.description: Stelow turns humans and AI agents into a cross-functional product team: research opportunity spaces, shape proposals with explicit trade-offs before code, plan typed scopes, and execute with gated reviews and agent workers. One board, one quiet inbox that only interrupts when you are needed.

sticky-prompt.description: Keeps your message pinned at the top of the chat, so you always know which question a long reply answers. As soon as your message scrolls up, a two-line copy stays above the reply, drawn with VesnALIA's own Markdown, and your next message pushes it away. Click it to jump back to the full message, even in a long thread where VesnALIA has unloaded it. Images show as thumbnails, short turns are left alone, and messages from agents and VesnALIA notices are skipped unless you turn them on. Runs in the VesnALIA app with your own session and needs no account or external service.

stl-preview.description: Inspect STL models beside your VesnALIA conversation. Orbit, pan and zoom, switch to wireframe, and read dimensions and triangle counts. Open workspace, host and thread-storage files through VesnALIA, including selected remote hosts. Requires WebGL2; supports binary and ASCII STL up to 64 MiB and one million triangles, with no separate viewer or external service.

subscription-pace.description: See whether every AI subscription you pay for will last until it renews. Tracks Vercel Token Pass and OpenCode Go live, and takes any other plan in the three free slots, then draws them all on one percent-of-allowance chart with a forecast to each renewal. There is no combined percentage: a headline that averages plans needs a weight for each, and OpenCode's limit is a per-model figure the endpoint does not name, so any weight would be a guess. Instead the panel counts the subscriptions in trouble — over the limit, or on pace to be before they reset. A provider that cannot be read shows as unreadable rather than as zero, and nothing is guessed: allowances start from a suggestion you confirm.

subscriptions.description: Get a short message in your thread when a GitHub pull request or Linear issue you follow changes. Subscribe from the agent or the VesnALIA subscriptions command, in bulk, and a count in the thread heading shows how many items you follow. Changes to a busy thread are coalesced into one message and rewritten in place, so a fast-moving issue never floods the queue. GitHub uses the gh CLI already authenticated on the VesnALIA server, and Linear needs one read-only personal API key.

subthread-columns.description: Answer waiting subthreads and inspect failures beside their parent. Optional Responsibilities adds unread-result columns.

super-diff.description: Read a long diff one concern at a time, with each group explained and notes under the lines a reviewer might misread. Click Generate Super Diff in the Diff tab, and the thread's agent groups the changed files into concerns in place of VesnALIA's file list, with a line on what each file's change does. Hover any other line, removed ones included, and click Explain this line for a note written on request. Each file keeps VesnALIA's Viewed checkbox, each concern counts its viewed files, and the list offers Regenerate when files change after it was written. Requires VesnALIA 0.48 or later; generating sends one message to the thread's agent.

switchboard.description: See which agent threads failed, need you or are still running, grouped under your VesnALIA sections. Child threads nest under their parent across projects, and a collapsed parent still shows its most urgent child. A status-lanes view lists every awake thread under Failed, Needs you, Running, Unread or Idle. Drag threads to reorder, nest or move them between sections, and snooze a quiet family until tomorrow morning. Hover a row for the thread's model, context use, branch, uncommitted changes and pull request. Choose Switchboard under Settings → Appearance → Sidebar in each VesnALIA client.

syns.description: Lets the pages your agents write read and save your Syns files, so a task board or wiki on a page is the repository itself, not a copy. A page sees only the repository, or the placed folder, its session works in, with the access of the Syns account signed in on that machine. Every edit carries the version the page last read: if the files moved since, the edit is refused and the page re-reads, so an edit never overwrites changes it hasn't seen. From a control you press, a page can also share a folder, set its visibility and manage who has access. Needs Thread Pages 1.10.0 or later, and the Syns CLI installed and signed in to a Syns account on each machine whose sessions use it.

system-messages-tab.description: Keeps "Your messages" in the thread outline to what you typed, moving VesnALIA notices and messages from other threads into their own tab. In an orchestrator thread with child agents, that took one outline from 1,045 entries to the 78 the user wrote. Every tab lists the newest message first, every outline entry gets a date and time, and senders the outline would label "Agent" show their thread title. A VesnALIA update can hide these changes until the plugin catches up; the outline keeps working.

t3-import.description: Bring your T3 Code threads into VesnALIA and pick up each conversation where you left off. Each thread lands in the VesnALIA project for its folder with its messages, reasoning, tool calls, plans, and dates, and the next message continues with the agent's full context. A preview lists every thread and project before anything changes, settled threads can come over archived, and each import backs up the VesnALIA database first. Requires VesnALIA 0.45, with T3 Code and Claude Code or Codex on the same computer; the plugin writes threads directly to the VesnALIA database.

t3sidebar.description: Replaces the VesnALIA thread list with a stable inbox, snooze controls, and child thread links.

tab-close-right.description: Keep tab icons visible and close tabs from the right. Active tabs always show their close button; other tabs reveal it on hover or keyboard focus without shifting the title. Touch screens show the button without hover. Requires VesnALIA 0.46.1+; future VesnALIA layout changes may require an update.

table-expand.description: Opens any markdown table in a thread full width, the way VesnALIA already expands images and Mermaid diagrams. Click the table or its corner expand button to see it in a dialog at the window width, with cells wrapping and both axes scrolling when it is still too big. Links, buttons and text selections inside the table keep working; Esc, the close button or the backdrop closes it. Relies on VesnALIA's table markup, so a VesnALIA update can break it until the plugin catches up.

tabs.description: Keep work and home conversations separate and return to the chats you need. Switch workspaces with independent pins and favorites, and restore your last local choice when reopening VesnALIA. Search chats and projects, explore nested chats in side menus, and customize project aliases and tab colors. Supports 15 interface languages; requires VesnALIA 0.43+ with no external service or account.

taskboard.description: Browses and creates project-scoped GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Linear, or Jira issues in one focused List or Kanban board, with explicit review before creation and an optional autonomous task factory.

tasks-kanban.description: Turn VesnALIA's built-in Tasks into a live Kanban board: drag cards across all six statuses, create, edit, comment, and label tasks. Every change goes straight into the Tasks tracker that VesnALIA tasks and agents use, so the board never drifts from the data. Works with any tracker project; Russian and English UI.

team.description: Agent teams with a shared Beads or built-in task tracker, reusable roles, safe session handoffs, review gates and finite execution budgets. Edit team templates, select approved models and follow task ownership and session status in one panel. Requires VesnALIA 0.49 or newer; Beads mode additionally requires bd 1.3.1.

telegram-projects.description: Get VesnALIA agent reports in Telegram and answer any thread from your phone, one topic per project. When an agent finishes, waits for you or stops, its project topic gets a card with the section, thread and agent, and the reply collapsed or summarized by a VesnALIA model you choose. Connect the reported thread with one tap and keep working with that agent by text or voice. Pick which agent and Tasks events arrive, with or without sound, and use the bot in Russian or English. Requires your own Telegram bot; messages of connected chats and reports are sent to Telegram.

terminal-jobs.description: Runs terminal commands that outlive agent turns, keeps job records and output logs, and sends completion notices to the owning VesnALIA thread.

terminal-toggle.description: Toggle the last focused native terminal with Ctrl+backtick. Press again to hide the panel and return to the composer.

terminals.description: Open shells on any machine connected to VesnALIA from one sidebar page, and find them still running when you come back. Each tab is a terminal in that machine's home folder, with no project, thread or checkout needed; with several machines connected, the + button lists them so you pick one. Tabs reattach to their shells after a reload, the desktop app and VesnALIA in a browser show and type into the same shells, and a machine that goes offline picks up where it was when it reconnects. Select text in a terminal to put it in an open or new thread's message box as terminal output, for you to send yourself. Requires VesnALIA 0.48 or later and at least one machine connected to VesnALIA; a terminal runs that machine's own shell as the user VesnALIA runs as there.

theme-glass.description: Turns VesnALIA's chrome into frosted glass over a soft mesh wallpaper, in light and dark mode. Sidebar, main pane, composer, popovers, dialogs, and cards become translucent sheets that keep text readable through the tint. No surface draws a border or shadow, so the window reads as one continuous material divided by tone alone. Works in the browser and the desktop app; requires backdrop-filter support and falls back to a solid palette without it.
theme-glass.licenseNote: в package.json указано "MIT", в репозитории permission

theme-toggle.description: Flips VesnALIA between light and dark from a sidebar footer button: a click switches the appearance, while hovering, holding, or right-clicking opens a menu with light, dark, or system appearance and every palette installed on the host, including ones other plugins provide. The icon is a square split by a diagonal — day above, night below — and the half that is on is filled.

thread-glow.description: Find threads after their agents stop working. See an orange highlight in the thread list and on open split-pane titles. Select a thread to clear its highlight. Middle-click an open pane title to close it.

thread-hover-cards.description: See what any thread or section is doing without opening it. Hover a thread in the sidebar for its status, model, run time, latest agent message, and pull request. Hover a section header to see open questions, failed runs, and unread threads without expanding it.

thread-images.description: Shows every image an agent opens right in the thread. Click one to see it full size. An Images gallery in the thread context card keeps every image from the thread, newest first. Works the same in Claude Code, Codex, ACP and Pi threads.

thread-namer.description: Names threads with an agent when their first turn ends, so the sidebar reads as what you were doing, and re-generates a name on demand from the thread header or the CLI.

thread-names.description: Names each thread "category: name" in lowercase, like "fix: login redirect loop", so a long sidebar reads at a glance. Eight categories for coding work come built in, and the settings page takes up to 16 of your own plus sample names in the style you want. Once you pick it as the thread-title service in VesnALIA settings, a thread whose title is not yet in that form gets a new one after a finished turn, at most twice. A thread you rename by hand after it got such a name keeps your title. Titles come from VesnALIA cloud, so the plugin needs a signed-in VesnALIA account with VesnALIA cloud on, and each title uses its daily AI budget; it needs no API key.

thread-nicknames.description: Identify threads by persistent numbers such as @27. New threads keep their number across title changes and reloads, while forks receive their own numbers. Browse numbered threads from the sidebar or Settings, then open one directly. Requires VesnALIA 0.42+; prefixes change actual thread titles and remain after disabling the plugin.

thread-pages.description: Gives every agent session a web page it writes for its task, and lets you answer from that page instead of chat. Each page is built for the task at hand: a diagram you click, a decision sheet, a report that shows what failed. Your choices and notes on the page arrive as the agent's next message, from VesnALIA or from your phone. A built-in home lists your sessions by what needs you and by project. Pages run sandboxed with no VesnALIA credentials, and anything that touches another session asks you first.

thread-reference.description: Bring a VesnALIA thread's current context into another conversation without copying its transcript. Drop a sidebar thread directly into the composer, or choose one from the Threads mention provider. References stay clickable in sent messages so you can return to the source thread. The plugin reads source threads without modifying them.

thread-reveal.description: Find the open thread in your sidebar without changing grouping or filters. Use the button beside its title or Ctrl+Shift+L (Command+Shift+L on macOS) to expand its branch, scroll to its row, and focus it. Reassign the shortcut in Settings. Requires VesnALIA 0.48.0+ and the built-in Thread list.

thread-switcher.description: Jump between your recent threads from the keyboard and see at a glance which one needs you. Hold Control and press Tab to step through a row of cards, each with the latest messages of that chat, its project, branch and status; let go to open the selected thread. On a phone, pinch two fingers together in a chat to open the same cards as a grid. A thread waiting for your answer shows the question it asked, and threads that need input or failed come first. A thread with subthreads counts how many are still running. The hotkey, the number of cards and the order are settings; no account or external service.

thread-tabs.description: Keep up to eight independent agent chats in one thread and workspace. Choose any installed model, fork an output into a transcript-backed tab, rename chats, and restore closed tabs. The output menu also keeps VesnALIA’s native fork into a separate thread. Requires VesnALIA 0.48.1 (0.48.x only) and your configured agent provider.

thread-tags.description: Puts a colored emoji or text badge before a thread's title, so you can spot status and topics in the sidebar at a glance. Tag a thread from the tag button in its hover controls, or create a tag there with up to 12 characters and a preset or custom color. An emoji picker lists every emoji by category and searches names in English and Russian, without network access. A Tags editor renames, recolors, and deletes tags, and the VesnALIA thread-tags command lets agents tag the thread they work in.

thread-time-machine.description: Step through everything an agent did in any thread, and diff its file changes between any two moments.Drag across a filmstrip of every message, command, file change and error, or press play, and open any frame to read its output, exit code or diff. Pin a start frame to see every file change between it and the current frame as diffs. Works on Codex, Claude Code, Pi, Muse Code, Cursor, opencode, Grok and Antigravity threads, including sub-agents, and adds frames live while an agent runs. A VesnALIA thread-time-machine dump command and a bundled agent skill print the same history as text. Read-only and local: no account or external service, and it never changes a thread.

thread-tree.description: See which agent spawned which thread. A sidebar thread list where child threads nest under the thread that started them, at any depth, and a parent folds its subtree into one line that counts each state. A search field on top (or /) finds threads by title, branch, PR number or project, above counts of threads that need input, failed, are running or are unread. Needs you collects threads asking a question, failed turns, threads stuck with no progress, unread results with their diff stat, failing PRs and failed automations, with Retry, Stop and snooze in place. Running rows show the current step, a turn timer and a high context fill. Orchestrations gives a shortcut to each thread running subthreads, with its progress. Provider subagents (Claude Code Agent calls, Codex subagents) show as a counter on the parent's row with type, state, duration and tokens on hover. Threads group by project or status and sort by last activity, creation date or status, with per-folder overrides; quiet threads fold into an "N older" line you can archive at once. Folded Pull requests (with the GitHub Folder plugin) and Automations sections summarize themselves in the header; hover a PR to merge it or start an agent review. Each row stays one line: VesnALIA's own status glyph, the title and the agent provider, plus a tinted PR icon only when the pull request needs action. A ⚠ marks a thread whose branch or worktree another live thread is using. Hovering a row shows Archive and its menu; hovering a running spinner lets you stop it. Reads thread data on the VesnALIA server; PR status comes from GitHub.

threadline.description: Jump to any point in a long conversation from a minimap of your own prompts. A slim rail on the right edge of a thread shows one marker per prompt you sent, and the current prompt stays highlighted as you scroll. Hover the rail to read each prompt's preview and click to jump straight to it, even when the message is far off-screen. Choose whether the rail sits at the top, middle, or bottom of the conversation. Runs entirely inside VesnALIA with no account or external service.

threadspace.description: Turns the VesnALIA sidebar into a Notion-style list of projects and threads. Give each project an emoji and a Notion background colour that fills its row. Pinned threads stay at the top of their own project, and threads waiting for your answer collect in one section above the projects. One status column shows running agents, questions, errors and unread results; collapsed projects show a count of work inside.

timer.description: Run floating focus timers, custom sprints, and pomodoro blocks anywhere in VesnALIA. Tracks multiple concurrent sessions with minute presets, draggable overlay positioning, and Web Audio completion chimes. Mounts as an app-wide overlay that collapses into a compact status pill and integrates with the thread header.

tinted-threads.description: A tinted replacement for VesnALIA's sidebar thread list with active and blocked row hues, provider glyphs, git diff badges, and sub-thread nesting.

token-guard.description: Stop API keys from landing in your agent chats, and find the ones already there. Rejects a message that contains a credential before it reaches the agent or thread history. Scans Claude Code, Codex and VesnALIA history on your server in one click. Lists each credential by kind and fingerprint with a link to its revoke page, and never shows, stores or sends a value.

token-pass-pace.description: See whether your Vercel Token Pass will last the billing period, before it runs out. A sidebar page charts every day of the period and projects your recent daily spend to the renewal date, naming the day you hit the limit. A footer line keeps the percentage and countdown in view. Needs a Vercel AI Gateway API key, your renewal day, and your allowance, entered once.

tokenmaxx.description: Shows every Codex and Claude Code account tokenmaxx manages, with live rate-limit windows, token analytics, account switching, auto-rotation policy, sign-in, and routing control.

tokenomics.description: See what your threads cost in tokens and time, and whether your subscription's session and weekly limits will last until they reset. Each thread's header shows a sparkline of its token use that opens a summary of which of your messages used the most tokens and time. VesnALIA's title bar shows how much of your session and week you have used, in amber or red when either is on pace to run out before it resets. Once a thread's context passes a size you set, a meter above the composer offers to compact it. A Tokenomics page charts tokens by hour or day, shows where turn time went, and ranks threads by use. Counts tokens, not dollars, needs VesnALIA 0.43 or later, and counts Claude Code subagents only for threads that ran on the same machine as VesnALIA.

tokyo-night.description: Adds the two Tokyo Night palettes (Night and Storm), each pairing its dark base with Tokyo Night Light for light mode.

top-tabs.description: Switch between the threads you are working on from a row of tabs across the top of the VesnALIA window. Every thread you open gets a tab with VesnALIA's status glyph, so a thread that is working, needs input, or has unread output shows without the sidebar. Close tabs with × or a middle-click, drag them to reorder, and cycle through them with Ctrl+Tab. Right-click a tab for VesnALIA's thread menu plus Close other tabs and Close tabs to the right. Tabs are stored per window on your machine, with no account or external service; requires VesnALIA 0.49 or later.

touchbar.description: Keep VesnALIA agent status and guarded controls on a MacBook Pro Touch Bar across every app. Open threads, follow provider usage, and switch to compact Host Monitor gauges. Requires macOS 11+, a Touch Bar Mac, and Xcode Command Line Tools; native mode uses Apple's private Touch Bar frameworks.

trace-mcp.description: See repository context and saved decisions beside every VesnALIA thread. Search code, record decisions, and reindex without leaving the thread. Native agent tools and VesnALIA trace commands keep queries compact. Runs on the environment's machine; first use needs Node.js and npm registry access. Shows provider context usage when VesnALIA reports it and does not alter quotas.

traces.description: Indexes local agent session files and opens searchable trajectories with message, tool, error, and provider filters.

tracing.description: See where every second of an agent turn went, one click from the answer it produced. A chip under each answer opens the turn on a timeline: every command, tool call, thinking block and response in its own color, with the full command, output, arguments or diff of any step. Silences become named steps: Generating shows what the model had just read and what it wrote next, and API retries shows failed provider calls with each backoff. Each turn records its token spend split into cache reads, cache writes, uncached input and output, and a Tracing page sums turn time, failures and tokens across threads. Spans are kept on the VesnALIA server as NDJSON files in OpenBot's trace format, and the VesnALIA tracing command answers the same questions for agents. Nothing leaves the VesnALIA server. Needs VesnALIA 0.48 or newer.

tree-sidebar.description: Find threads by where their project lives on disk: folders nest, projects sit inside them, and each thread sits under its project. Forks and side chats nest under the thread they came from. Search reads message text as well as titles, shows the matching line under each result, and lists archived matches in their own section. Hover a thread to archive it in one click, or right-click it to open it in a split, copy its link, pin it, or delete it. Optional settings sort VesnALIA's project list and indent its new-thread project picker to match the tree.

treehouse.description: Review, edit and commit every repository your agents touched, worktrees included, from a split panel beside the thread. Files, diffs and commits open as tabs next to a file tree with git badges, and you can edit a file and save it with Ctrl/⌘+S. Each repository gets staged and unstaged lists, per-hunk staging, and a commit box where Claude can write the message in your repo's style. Compare any branch with main and open a pull request on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket, or click a commit in the branch graph to see its diff. Needs git on the thread's machine; the commit-message button also needs an Anthropic API key, an ant login or the claude CLI.

treelanes.description: Take each coding task from idea to merged pull request in its own Git worktree, with checks before every stage moves. A board shows one card per worktree as agents move it through Design, TDD, Quality Loop, Simplify and PR Watch. A stage moves on only when its worker reports passing checks for the current files. The sidebar lists one main thread per worktree, with its other threads below it. The task map sets the harness, model and effort for each step. Needs an agent harness such as Claude Code or Codex, and the GitHub CLI for pull requests.

triage.description: Keep agent tasks, progress, and work that needs your attention in one board. Run tasks now or schedule them, organize stages, and turn existing sessions into cards. Follow each task in its linked conversation. Requires VesnALIA 0.42+, a compatible Plugin SDK 0.4.47 runtime, and a configured agent provider; provider usage charges apply.

try-it.description: Test what your agent built from your phone, and send your verdict back with one tap per check. The agent shows a QR code, a link, what changed and a checklist in place of the composer. Each check gets Works or Broken, plus an optional note, and the answer goes straight back to the agent. Localhost links are refused, so the link you get opens on your phone.

turn-tps.description: Show tokens per second on every completed turn, so a slow answer is visible without opening a log. Each finished turn gets a badge under the assistant message with output tokens, wall-clock duration, and the resulting rate, and the turn header carries the same figure in short form. Reads usage the provider reports where VesnALIA has it, and the local OMP session file for ACP and OMP threads, which report none. The rate divides output tokens by the full turn duration, so tool calls and provider waits count against it; it is not a model decode benchmark. Needs a completed turn, and the ACP and OMP path needs that thread's OMP session file on the machine running VesnALIA.

typewriter.description: Hear IBM Selectric clicks as you type in VesnALIA, with five WAV sounds included. Set the volume, preview Enter or import a personal sound pack stored only on your device. No account, external service or OS keyboard-monitoring permission is needed.

typography.description: Set your own interface and code fonts in VesnALIA, down to size, line height, bold weight, and OpenType features. Interface size and line height scale the theme's whole type ramp, so headings and labels keep their proportions. Code settings reach inline code, code blocks, the source viewer, and diffs. A preview built from VesnALIA's own chat and source renderers shows each saved change, and every value also works from VesnALIA plugin config. Fonts must already be installed on the device that displays VesnALIA.

ui-scale.description: Makes the VesnALIA interface bigger or smaller on each device, so your phone and desktop each get a size that fits. A slider from 50% to 200% scales text, spacing, and layout, and the change applies immediately. Each browser and phone keeps its own value, stored locally and never synced. On iOS, it also stops Safari from zooming in when you tap a text field.

ui-tweaks.description: Tune VesnALIA's type, icons, prompt box, menus and shortcuts with switches that VesnALIA itself does not offer. Clearer hierarchy, on by default, makes thread titles bolder and chat text slightly larger. Switch interface icons between VesnALIA Default, Lucide, Iconoir and Tabler Outline, and give the spinner its own style. Move the new-thread prompt to the top, center or bottom, hide Steer labels, turn on richer File Editor highlighting, and hide apps from the Open With menu. Alt+1 to Alt+9 switch right-panel tabs, and settings are saved on the VesnALIA server so every device shares them. Needs VesnALIA 0.49 or newer; no account or external service.

ultra-launcher.description: Start a VesnALIA thread from any screen with Cmd+N, without leaving the thread you are in. Each thread starts from a saved preset of provider, model, reasoning level and service tier. Enter opens the new thread, and Cmd+Enter starts it in the background with an Open button in a toast. Save up to 30 presets, reorder them by dragging, and edit them in the picker or in settings. On phones the launcher opens as a bottom sheet. It takes over Cmd+N and moves VesnALIA's own New thread shortcut to Cmd+Shift+O, and one setting gives Cmd+N back. Requires VesnALIA 0.46 or later.

ultragoal.description: Keep long-running agent work moving without losing the plan when a thread ends. UltraGoal schedules dependency-ready slices across isolated workers, records defects and owner decisions durably, and can require an independent verifier before work closes. Each goal pins worker and verifier execution settings, reports host substitutions, and can replace idle clean workers one at a time. Repository integration, worktree cleanup, and local provider-data reads stay off until you enable them. Requires VesnALIA 0.39+ and Plugin SDK 0.4.8+.

unified-inbox.description: Read Gmail, WhatsApp, Messages, and LinkedIn in one list beside the thread. Reply where that source can send, and mute a conversation without removing it. A mail image shows in the message, and a shared LinkedIn post shows its words and picture. Gmail needs your own Google Cloud client, WhatsApp pairs as a linked device, LinkedIn uses this plugin's Chrome window, and Messages needs imsg plus Full Disk Access on a Mac.

unslop.description: Agent-invoked filter — the agent can strip overused AI patterns like hedging, filler, and corporate affect from text before sending.

uptime.description: Monitor website availability and response times from your VesnALIA server. View recent checks and see when a site is down. Requires the server to remain running and able to reach the sites.

usage.description: Tracks coding-agent token usage and estimated API cost across enrolled machines.

usage-bar.description: Keep provider quotas and reset times above the sidebar footer. Open quota details and inspect daily and monthly token totals. Requires providers that report usage to VesnALIA; Usage Limits is optional.

usage-forecast.description: Forecast whether your Claude Code and Codex limits last until reset, and see each thread's context fill above the composer. A band shows every limit window with a pace tick, the context breakdown and a Compact button, and adds a learned forecast once windows have closed. Optional auto-compact, off by default, compacts an idle thread above a threshold you set; each compact runs a turn on the thread's provider and counts against its limits. Limits appear only for providers that report them to VesnALIA, today Claude Code and Codex. The server polls VesnALIA every 2 minutes and calls no provider API.

usage-limits.description: See provider quota windows and reset times without leaving your work. View details across connected hosts and refresh on demand. Requires providers that report quota information to VesnALIA.

usage-meter.description: Shows Claude subscription limits as two rings around a sidebar footer button — the five-hour session and the week — and adds a Usage page that reads local Claude Code transcripts to explain where the limits went, broken down by project, model, thread, skill and subagent.

usage-pace.description: Tells you if your current rate lasts until each quota window resets. In VesnALIA's usage card, each bar gets a tick at even pace, and red shows how far ahead of pace you are. Hover or tap a row to see the difference, when the quota runs out, and how long you will be without quota before the reset. Adds a Grok Build tab, shows a failed provider's error on its own tab only, and hides tabs you do not use, such as Cursor. The Grok tab reads your grok login and asks xAI's billing service for the credit window; everything else uses the data VesnALIA's card already has.

usage-page.description: Tracks Claude Code, Codex, and Pi token usage with estimated API costs in a VesnALIA dashboard.

usage-tracker.description: See subscription limits without leaving VesnALIA. Track Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Antigravity, and DeepSeek in a compact sidebar summary with provider details and 80/95% warnings.

vantage.description: See every worktree your parallel agents work in, and everything they changed across repositories, from the parent thread. Each worktree shows status, branch, commits ahead and behind, uncommitted files and its pull request; open one to read its diffs and commits, talk to its agent, or start a terminal in it. Files changed in two worktrees are flagged before they conflict. A full-screen Vantage page in VesnALIA's left navigation shows every recent thread's worktrees and changed repositories at once, filtered by project. It paints at once and loads git details in the background; archived threads stay hidden on the page until you ask for them.

variaq.description: Run VariaQ classical/quantum experiments from VesnALIA. Generate problems, solve, benchmark, plan and execute campaigns, analyze results, and generate reports against a standalone VariaQ install. Supports VariaQ 0.6.x and 0.8.x including 0.8.0rc1; schema-v1 validated. Requires VesnALIA and a separate VariaQ install.

vcs-widget.description: Run Git from the VesnALIA thread header instead of a terminal: branches, commits and history, on the machine that owns the worktree. Every push, rebase and reset shows the exact git command before it runs.

vercel-theme.description: Adds a Vercel-inspired light and dark palette with Geist typography and matching code, diff, file-tree, and terminal colors.

vesnalia-agent-toolbox.description: Gives any coding agent (opencode, Prime Agent, Google Antigravity, Codex, Claude Code, and more) direct tools for VesnALIA: read and edit workspace files, inspect and message other threads, delegate work by spawning threads, and see running terminals.

vesnalia-bbs.description: Dial into a 1994-style bulletin board from VesnALIA to chat with other VesnALIA users and play classic multiplayer door games. Doors include Legend of the Red Dragon, Trade Wars 2, Usurper and Dice Warz, in shared worlds with daily turns and leaderboards. Your first call creates an account from a handle and a silly questionnaire; VesnALIA keeps the password, so there is no email or GitHub sign-in. Opted-in agents get their own [BOT] account and two tools to read the screen and press keys, limited to one chat line per 30 seconds and no board posts. Connects to the community server at bbs.gravytrain.ca, run by the author.

vesnalia-box.description: Give each thread its own Linux, Windows or macOS computer, or an iPhone or Android device, shared with its agent. You and the agent use the same desktop or terminal in VesnALIA's panel, and the agent waits while you have control. On the backends that support it, a snapshot saves a box before a risky change, and a restore with an undo or a fork brings it back. Boxes run on Docker, microsandbox, Proxmox, Tart on your Macs, or your own machines over SSH; Hetzner Cloud, Namespace and boat.dev need an account and bill you for what boxes use. Not a sandbox: VesnALIA Box assumes one trusted user.

vesnalia-live.description: Talk to VesnALIA while your agents work, then redirect threads or start new project work by voice. Keeps one voice session connected while you move through projects, focus threads, and hear task results in the transcript. Explicit new tasks can start project threads or go to the VesnALIA Operator for coordination, while consequential actions stay in VesnALIA's visual approval flow. Requires VesnALIA 0.43.1+, Git, npm, Node.js 22.19+, an OpenAI project with GPT-Live access, and microphone permission; OpenAI usage is billed separately.

vesnalia-office.description: Turns active VesnALIA threads into a draggable pixel-art office with live worker state, thread navigation, usage indicators, and agent-configurable behavior.

vesnalia-sidebar.description: A sidebar inspired by T3 Code that adds manual and automatic thread sorting, collapsible shelves, and bulk actions to VesnALIA.

vesper.description: Recolor VesnALIA, its diffs and its terminal in Vesper's peppermint and orange. Pick Vesper to follow VesnALIA's light or dark mode, or Vesper Dark or Vesper Light to keep one look. Diffs and file previews use Vesper's syntax colors, and the dark code theme is the original Vesper file. The plugin adds only CSS and color files and runs nothing in the background. Requires VesnALIA 0.46 or later.

vim.description: Write VesnALIA prompts with Vim motions, modes, selections, and operators while VesnALIA keeps its native composer behavior. Insert mode leaves attachments, image paste, model controls, voice input, and submission to VesnALIA. Normal, Visual, and Visual Line modes add counts, text objects, search, yank, paste, undo, and redo. Terminals, search fields, command palettes, and opted-out plugin surfaces stay native. Requires VesnALIA 0.41+ and Plugin SDK 0.4.34+; no external service or paid account is required.

visual-workflows.description: Connect specialist steps on a canvas and follow their outputs through each run. Includes local step profiles and can import independent copies from Agent Roles. Runs use your configured providers and their quotas.

voice-input.description: Dictate into any VesnALIA chat and get clean text back, with your product names spelled right. Choose which machine does the recognition: Whisper (MLX) and GigaAM v3 keep the audio on that machine, while Groq, OpenAI and Google transcribe in the cloud with your own API key. A term vocabulary repairs garbled product and tool names, and an optional AI pass fixes the ones the rules miss. Recordings are written to disk before transcription, so a failed run never loses what you said. Local engines need Python 3, ffmpeg and macOS on Apple silicon; cloud engines need a paid API key.

voice-mode.description: Talk to a thread's agent hands-free, like ChatGPT or Codex voice. When the composer is empty its send button becomes a waveform; click it, or press Ctrl+Shift+V, for a full-duplex realtime voice chat. The voice model hands requests to the thread's agent, answers "is it done?", stops the agent when you say stop, and reads back a short summary when the turn ends. Talk over it any time to interrupt. Uses OpenAI Realtime with your own API key, or a plugin that provides realtime connections (for example a company AI proxy). VesnALIA's own send and dictation are never affected.

vps-watch.description: Keep an eye on your personal Linux VPS without installing a monitoring stack. See CPU, RAM, root disk and inode usage with absolute capacities and compact history charts. Read system counters over SSH or import an existing collector history without running duplicate measurements; the optional collector caps VPS history at 32 MiB. Requires SSH key access to Linux; optional background collection requires a separate Python 3 and Docker systemd setup, with no paid service or external API.

vscode-server.description: Embeds a self-hosted code-server or VS Code Server in a thread's right panel, opened at that thread's workspace so the editor shows the same files the agent is working on. One panel per thread, a compact header with the server URL and an Open in Browser link, and — for a loopback server — import of your desktop VS Code profile, keybindings, and extensions into it. You bring the server; the plugin embeds it and never proxies or weakens its authentication.

waiting-on-you.description: Shows which agent threads wait on your answer or failed, pinned above your thread list, so none of them sit unnoticed. Open one with a click, ⇧⌘J for the next, or ⌥⌘1–9 by its row; a thread leaves the block once you open it. Each question shows when it was asked, and counters in the title track waiting, failed, finished, and working threads. Pick a style, or tune markers, colors, row layout, and row limits on a settings page with a live preview, then move the setup between machines as JSON. Runs on your VesnALIA server only, with no account, API key, or outside service.

wakatime.description: Tracks VesnALIA agent working time locally with project, machine, model, concurrency, and activity breakdowns.

web-push-notify.description: Sends browser notifications when VesnALIA agents finish or fail, even while VesnALIA is closed.

wiki.description: Gives your agents a wiki of Markdown notes, so what one thread learns the next one can find. Agents search, cite and save notes with two tools, and each new thread starts with up to three notes that fit its first message. Citations open the note in the side panel and preview it on hover, and an @ mention adds a whole note as context. A Wiki panel lists the notes linked to the thread, and one button saves what's worth keeping and archives the thread. Needs a local folder of Markdown notes. git and mempalace are optional.

wikilinks.description: Edit Markdown notes in VesnALIA with wikilinks, recursive previews, contextual backlinks, and queryable thinking trails.

wizbar.description: An agent-first sidebar for fleets of agent threads. Cards show the issue or pull request link and child count, children open from a hover list, a live running count sits below the list with a stats panel on the footer bolt, drag pins and reorders, and every WizBar action has a wizbar CLI command with JSON. Derived from T3 Sidebar.

work-map.description: Spot the work that needs you and manage it without leaving the map. Expand tasks and sessions in place, keep pinned work prominent, and follow running agents and results waiting for you. Start or continue sessions, manage project areas, and leave task handoffs with Undo. Requires VesnALIA 0.43 or later and its built-in Tasks plugin; sessions use your chosen VesnALIA provider and its usual account requirements and costs.

workbench-explorer.description: Keeps a file tree beside every thread that shows what the agent changed in git colours, one click away from the diff. Quick Open finds any file from a few letters of its name, and Search in Files previews every replacement before it is written. The tree works from the keyboard: arrows, F2 to rename, Delete to move to the Trash with Undo, and Cut, Copy and Paste for files; drag and drop moves them. Files open in VesnALIA's own editor, with Material Icon Theme icons. Git colours and diffs need a git repository; the Trash works on macOS and Linux.

workspace-sidebar.description: Keep every VesnALIA thread visible as work moves across projects. Group threads by project or status, pin current work, and see subagents nested under their parent. Review pull requests, branches, failures, and scheduled work on each row. Select threads in batches to move, snooze, or finish them, and use VesnALIA sidebar from a terminal. Replaces VesnALIA's thread list and requires VesnALIA 0.46 or later.

workspace-skills.description: Connect external skill repositories and workspace folders directly to VesnALIA without hardcoding paths or copying files. Discovers nested skill packages across your configured directories and registers them into VesnALIA's shared skill roots. Discovered skills appear in the slash menu and session instructions across all projects and providers. Configure paths via Settings or the workspace-skills CLI subcommand. Changes to skills in their source repositories reflect immediately without re-installing.

workspaces.description: Run one agent thread across several repositories, each in its own isolated Git worktree. Group existing VesnALIA projects into a reusable workspace, then select only the repositories a task needs and start a thread rooted at all of them. Every checkout branches from its repository's own default branch, and your source clones are never pulled, checked out, or stashed. The thread's Repositories panel reports changed files and commits ahead for each checkout, and can enroll another project mid-session. Removing worktrees requires an archived session with every checkout clean and still on its recorded branch, and generated branches are never deleted. Uses local Git and VesnALIA's public plugin APIs, with no account, token, or external service.

worktree-ports.description: See which port each worktree's dev server is on, and open it in one click. The app port leads as a named pill; database, Docker, and internal listeners fold behind a toggle so nothing is hunted for. Hover a pill to stop the process or container holding it. The same listing answers `alia ports list` and the worktree_ports agent tool, so an agent can name the URL instead of guessing. Needs lsof, so macOS or Linux only; Docker ports need the docker CLI.

worktree-setup.description: Runs per-repo setup scripts when VesnALIA creates a worktree, using a global git post-checkout hook so nothing needs to live in your repositories.

wterm-terminal-preview.description: Adds a Ghostty-backed terminal with independent tabs, TUI mouse input, secure file transfer, and font controls.

x-viral.description: Scores a draft X post against the open-source For You ranking weights, then runs an autoresearch loop that applies every edit that raises the score, checks dropped images and videos for the feed, and drafts a video script.

xberg.description: Lets agents read the PDFs, Word files, spreadsheets, slides and images in your project. Documents are converted on the machine that holds the workspace, and the plugin uploads no files, though the extracted text reaches the agent's model. OCR reads text in images, and can be turned on for scanned documents. Long documents come back in pages of 20,000 characters by default, and the agent chooses how many to read. First use downloads the open-source Xberg CLI (50–90 MB) from GitHub; it needs 120–230 MB of disk plus caches, of up to 2 GB for text and no set limit for OCR, and runs only on Apple Silicon macOS and Linux.

xcode.description: Tracks every Xcode build and test on the machine with no per-project configuration — live progress, verdicts, errors with file:line, history and trends — and streams the simulators they run on into the panel with full touch input, a build-aware device picker, SwiftUI preview diffs, and gated agent tools.

xlsx-preview.description: Read Excel workbooks directly in VesnALIA’s file panel. Switch between sheets and view merged cells, dates, and up to 1,000 rows × 100 columns per sheet. Find workbooks in your workspace and thread files from the Spreadsheets button. Supports .xlsx and .xlsm without an external account or separate spreadsheet application.

zcode.description: Run ZCode coding agents inside VesnALIA, with streamed replies, native tool activity, approvals, and sessions you can resume and rewind. Follow every ZCode tool call in the thread timeline, answer approvals inline, and track background agents and scheduled automations. Dynamic workflows render as causality graphs with live per-agent progress, and a Workflows hub lists run history across threads. Requires VesnALIA 0.46.1, Node.js 24+, and the ZCode CLI installed separately; sessions run under your own Z.ai Coding Plan or API account, billed by Z.ai. Verified on macOS against ZCode CLI 0.16.9-0.17.0; Linux and Windows are unverified.

zcode-acp.description: Use your ZCode Coding Plan, free Start Plan and personal API models in VesnALIA. Install or update Rust ACP in settings and track each plan's quota separately. Requires VesnALIA 0.49+ and a signed-in ZCode Desktop installation on Windows or macOS. Coding Plan requires a paid subscription; personal API charges follow your provider, while Start Plan depends on an active free grant.

zcode-provider.description: Use your Z.ai GLM Coding Plan for coding tasks in VesnALIA on macOS. Choose GLM-5.3 or GLM-5.3-Flash, work with files and terminal tools, and continue saved sessions through your installed ZCode agent. Reuse Desktop sign-in and its shared store, settings and configured MCP servers; VesnALIA sessions, history and logs stay separate. Requires Apple silicon, VesnALIA 0.47.1+, Git, ZCode Desktop, an individual paid Z.ai Coding Plan and Full permissions; unofficial and unaffiliated with Z.ai, ZCode or VesnALIA.

zen-koi.description: Watch pixel-art koi swim under your chat input while the agent works, and scoop them in a one-tap catch game. When a ! shows over the paper poi, tap to lift that koi into the bowl; leave it alone and the poi plays by itself. Draw up to nine koi that grow from 15 to 45 cm over two weeks, and set the garden, season, time of day, and rain. Optional sound adds water, a wind chime, and rain in a soft reverb. Your koi and catch counts stay on your VesnALIA server and use no external service.

zh-cn.description: Use Simplified Chinese across VesnALIA menus, settings and built-in panels while keeping project, thread and Git. Includes 5,914 translated strings and preserves dynamic names and placeholders. Chat content, code, terminals and recognized custom titles keep their original text; disabling the plugin restores the interface. Runs locally without a translation API or account; the dictionary targets VesnALIA 0.49.0 and requires VesnALIA 0.49+.
